# Nathan Magsig Declares Victory in Senate District 12
---
|
---
| | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** November 10th, 2026Contact: nathan@nathanmagsig.com
---
| | | | | |
**Nathan Magsig Declares Victory in Senate District 12**
**FRESNO, CA** – Today, Nathan Magsig declared victory in California’s 12th State Senate District. The Associated Press has also called the race for Magsig.
“I am honored by the trust the voters of Senate District 12 have placed in me,” said Magsig. “Throughout this campaign, I heard from families struggling with rising costs, farmers who need reliable water supplies, and communities concerned about crime, wildfire, and the availability of insurance. I am ready to take those concerns to Sacramento and fight for the people who call this district home.”
Magsig campaigned on lowering costs, strengthening public safety, securing reliable water supplies, and improving forest management. He will bring his experience as a Fresno County Supervisor, former Clovis Mayor, and small business owner to the State Senate.
“I want to thank my Lord and savior Jesus Christ, my family, our volunteers, and every supporter who knocked on doors, made calls, put up a sign, or shared our message,” Magsig continued. “This victory reflects the hard work of so many people who believe our communities deserve a stronger voice in Sacramento.”
“To everyone in Senate District 12, whether you voted for me or not, I will work hard to earn your trust. I look forward to serving you and delivering results for our Valley and mountain communities.”
---
| | ###
Senator-Elect Nathan Magsig is a current Fresno County Supervisor and former Mayor of Clovis. His family, wife Julie and their three children, reside in Clovis, CA.

# [](https://act.electjon.com/go/4629?t=1&akid=3269%2E5691347%2EZKsmk0)

Peter,
Last week, in sweeping and decisive victories, the American people rebuked the depravity, corruption, and incompetence of the failed lame duck President Donald J. Trump.
But, Peter, amidst our celebration, we must acknowledge that the underlying crisis gripping our Republic remains — and that therefore our most vital work lies ahead.
[**Right now, while the wind is at our back, I’m asking for $5 or whatever you can give to help carry our historic movement forward. We still need you, Peter.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-nov26.ijcilw&refcode=em261110-1-f-c&utm_campaign=em261110-1-f-c&amount=5&t=2&akid=3269%2E5691347%2EZKsmk0)
**[CONTRIBUTE $5](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-nov26.ijcilw&refcode=em261110-1-f-c&utm_campaign=em261110-1-f-c&amount=5&t=3&akid=3269%2E5691347%2EZKsmk0)**
Our work isn’t finished yet, Peter.
While the wealthy and well-lobbied feast on inside information and official favors, America's forgotten families face systemic corporate disrespect and official indifference, working harder and harder while the treadmill just gets faster and steeper, and the bills get higher and higher.
Instead of reading your daughter her favorite book that precious spare hour after work, you're on the phone begging the insurance company to cover the medicine that prevents her seizures.
You report the black mold to your landlord, who doesn't fix the leak, and the ambulance for your toddler's asthma attack is followed by a $3,000 bill.
For too many, home ownership’s a fantasy. Family farms face ruin. And while health care’s never cost more, plastics invade our bodies, blood, and breast milk. Toxic forever chemicals taint half the country's drinking water, and polluters have been granted fresh license to poison our air.
You’ve seen that abroad, American credibility and leadership are in decay while the world re-arms for global conflict.
You see that at our grave peril, humanity is fast forgetting the terrible lessons of two World Wars and the Holocaust.
Meanwhile, you see the titans of Silicon Valley digging bunkers for themselves and warning that the artificial intelligence they're creating risks human extinction.
And amidst these challenges of unprecedented consequence and complexity, though we rightly celebrate this historic victory, the fact is we’ve been too long mired in a small and selfish politics — a politics bought by big money, unmoored from fixed moral principles, and resigned to intractable division.
In other words, the United States has been adrift in a gale.
But we can and will reclaim control over our own destiny — not just through this historic landslide victory, but through all the vital work that follows it.
You know that my team’s work doesn’t end just because we’ve won the election. We still have bills to pay and we still need your help to keep building this movement.
[**I know it’s a lot to ask after a grueling cycle, but if you’re able, please donate whatever you can today. Our work is far from over.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-nov26.ijcilw&refcode=em261110-1-f-c&utm_campaign=em261110-1-f-c&t=4&akid=3269%2E5691347%2EZKsmk0)
**[CONTRIBUTE $5](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-nov26.ijcilw&refcode=em261110-1-f-c&utm_campaign=em261110-1-f-c&amount=5&t=5&akid=3269%2E5691347%2EZKsmk0)**
Thanks for continuing to be part of this team,
Jon

name: Coach Tommy Tuberville
subject: Thank you!
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY TUBERVILLE FOR GOVERNOR, INC
body:
We Won!
| Peter,

**We Won!**
[](http://links.tubervilleforalabama.com/u/click?_t=b8b4efbe79f64b579dfa7d8da685a7a9&_m=2e058647f35142d0b8b0247df4436bc4&_e=4fQknZsi46KXyD1GAVvhdmu1Vw2_KarEkj1npq9TUXQcuELw4jJldEXlHX6VEV9k8VVXN4Tu67d9OmAbKO7ZKpqCkFEQIMzer8Xv3JGKH5mbN5f9oCPywEimv7Tl3t13YlExqWVysgZEScqohznPXN4Le4rP7qa0cC_AaJIG3FyxDerFmX8nMONm5qgJ_ipBTNuMP7BzHycpixBAuhb-RK9YgmEI9YzXUyqGVeILq-OCAtNvKfjQTU6WHjacVXXpOYe8bwNmgVT80lgYuc-1gj_8NZR3YMxpYGhIlXKvfmyZkv3IYxiTGVUWvCUnGErauLMPd3YhzIRKGmWS-ewmqsNecun08eaQrhtxkU_0esV9iEsuEvCSvKKhl66l1EJZYe95WEBR8w5YteHWufBLjrItY88Xs-dbeKd1pbNWe_1z634M_dV9Rnl_EAgMrBgACmPg8q95F6pswQFstR418_ZOA8dt2NsniJi7NtetELU8XaSSukr-eDti-fk0WjBPpvLPqob6fW9wEuvsIvRrs0s9MmgoHRHvOL65JKMA3TI%3D)
_I want to start by saying thank you, from the bottom of my heart._ _**I love this state, and I’m honored to serve as Alabama’s 55th Governor.**_

_This campaign was never about me. It was about Alabama. It was about people who believe this state should put its citizens first, protect its values, and make its own decisions, not let Washington make them for us.

You showed up. You worked. You voted. And because of you, we’re moving forward together.

I’ve been a coach most of my life, and I’ve been in a lot of locker rooms after big wins. The best ones aren’t where people celebrate the loudest. They’re where everybody understands the work that got them there.

That’s how I feel today.

There’s a lot of work ahead, and I don’t take it lightly. I’ll be governor for every Alabamian, whether they voted for me or not. And we’re starting from a position of strength because of the people who stood with this campaign from day one._

_**Thank you for your trust.
Thank you for your support.
Thank you for believing that Alabama’s best days are still ahead.**_

_I’m ready to get to work.

God bless,
Coach Tommy Tuberville _

name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: President AOC? It's not a joke anymore.
body:
Plus: New Mexico Democrats hit the supermajority | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/10NN6ZPuuZu?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | |
Last Tuesday was brutal. No way around it.
[So this week I brought in Republican pollster Jeff Glassburner to tell us what actually happened.](https://us.list-manage.com/kb8aCAlifju?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e) Independents didn’t just lean left, they voted like Democrats. New Mexico now has a 47-23 supermajority in the House. And the Senate isn’t coming back for a while.
Then I asked Jeff which Democrat worries him most in 2028. He said AOC
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/7JqRRPGmBKm?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| |
**🔥 INDEPENDENTS DIDN’T LEAN DEMOCRAT. THEY VOTED LIKE DEMOCRATS.**
Pollsters nailed where Republicans would land. Then the undecideds broke 30, 40, 50 points the other way, depending on the state. Jeff says independents haven’t voted as one bloc like this since Watergate.
This was not a turnout collapse. Jeff explains what it was instead, and why that’s harder to fix.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/32gbEne4MGt?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
**🚨 JD VANCE SAYS IT WAS IRAN. JEFF SAYS LOOK AT LAST YEAR.**
The vice president blamed the war this week. Jeff points to two governor’s races a full year ago that showed the same number everyone’s shocked by now.
Republicans lost Mississippi, Kansas and Texas on the same night. Jeff has one line about what that means for the party that I couldn’t argue with either.

**🏛️ DEMOCRATS NOW HAVE A SUPERMAJORITY IN SANTA FE.**
Rebecca Dow is out. Luis Terrazas is out. Democrats hold exactly two-thirds of the New Mexico House.
I pulled Eddy, Lea and Chaves County turnout and compared it to 2022. The population went up. Republican turnout went the other way.
There’s also a registration number that changes how we look at 2030.

**⚠️ PRESIDENT AOC. IT’S NO JOKE.**
Jeff says Republicans are underestimating AOC “to an extreme degree.” She’s going to own the rooms in Iowa, South Carolina and Nevada, and the center of the Democratic Party has nobody left who can box her out the way Biden boxed out Bernie.
Then we walk through the 2028 Senate map. Six seats, none of them deep red, and a road back that probably runs through 2030.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/Qn5vvWFREA3?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
**PLUS:** Why Trump “likes it when his proteges fight,” 65 House seats in play for 2028, Jeff’s three-word advice for the White House, and the prediction bet Krysty lost. Ella may not get dinner this week.
---
|
---

Pennsylvania is home to over 600,000

courage, honor, and integrity.

remember our nation’s veterans, I want to extend my sincere gratitude to

Thank you for your commitment to service and our Constitution.

Thank you for having our backs. I promise, I’ll always have yours.

Wishing you a happy Veterans Day,

Josh Shapiro

subject: Happy Veterans Day, Michigan
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JOCELYN BENSON FOR GOVERNOR]
body:
[ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
Happy Veterans Day, Michigan.

As the wife of a combat veteran, I’ve seen firsthand the sacrifices our
military service members, their families, and veterans make every single
day.

To Michigan’s hundreds of thousands of veterans: Thank you for your
service. We honor you, and we’re committed to supporting you and your
families every day.

I know we have a long way to go to ensure every Michigan veteran has
access to healthcare, to mental health support, and to housing, but I can
tell you this: we’ll always go above and beyond to serve and support our
veterans. They’re our community too.

As your Governor, I’ll use every tool in my toolbox to make sure we’re
serving and protecting those who served and protected us.

Happy Veterans Day, Michigan.

Gratefully,
Jocelyn Benson

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is a critical way we communicate with supporters like you.

name: Tim Walz
subject: Proud to have served
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Small Town PAC, [smalltownpac
body:
Today, I’m thinking about my fellow veterans and the families who stand beside them.
#
Peter,
Two days after my 17th birthday, my dad drove me to meet a lieutenant who had a farm near our house. He got off his tractor to administer my oath of enlistment right there in his cornfield.
Raising my right hand to join the National Guard was one of the best decisions I ever made. I was proud to wear our country’s uniform for the next 24 years.
During those years, I learned a lot about hard work, service, and looking out for the people beside you. Those lessons have stayed with me ever since.
Today, on Veterans Day, I’m thinking about everyone who has answered that call to serve, along with the families who have stood beside them through long absences, uncertainty, and sacrifice.
**We owe them more than a thank-you. We owe them the care and support they’ve earned, long after they take off the uniform.** That means access to health care, a safe place to call home, and a community that has their back.
If there’s a veteran in your life, reach out today. Ask how they’re doing. Let them know you’re thinking of them. And let’s keep looking out for them the other 364 days of the year, too.
To my fellow veterans and your families: Thank you. It’s an honor to stand with you.
Tim

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: In words, and in actions
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20261111-6951-footer&t=1001&akid=6951%2E420207%2EZdNP_k ]Pramila Jayapal

Peter,

Today, we honor the veterans who put their lives on the line to defend our
democracy.

They kept their promise to our country. Now we must keep ours to them.

That means more than words. It means ensuring every veteran can access the
physical and mental health care they need. It means opening doors to
higher education and good-paying jobs. And it means making sure every
veteran can afford a safe, stable, and dignified life after service.

Our veterans showed up for us. We must show up for them — with the care,
support, and respect they have earned.

And that commitment must extend to the servicemembers currently being put
in harm’s way. We cannot honor those who have served while ignoring the
lives of those being asked to fight in Trump's war of choice in Iran.

This war is a disgrace, both to our nation and to our servicemembers.

It benefits no one, it was never authorized by Congress, and it is a
dangerous abuse of power by the President. Our servicemembers took an oath
to defend this country — not to risk their lives in an unconstitutional
war launched by a president who refuses to serve the needs of the American
people.

I will keep fighting to end this war and restore Congress’ constitutional
power over war and peace. The results of last Tuesday’s election make
clear that the American people expect accountability, and I intend to
deliver it.

And to every veteran, servicemember, and military family reading this:
thank you, thank you, thank you. I am sincerely grateful for your service
and your sacrifice.

In solidarity,

Pramila Jayapal

name: Squad Victory Fund
subject: Honoring our veterans today
body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20261111-2929-foote&t=1001&akid=2929%2E342411%2EOwb99u ]Squad Victory Fund

Happy Veterans Day,
Peter.

Today, we honor the millions of Americans who answered the call to serve.

They put their lives on hold, and often on the line, to protect our
country, our freedoms, and our communities. And so many military families
made sacrifices right alongside them.

Every one of them deserves a country that keeps its promises: quality
health care, mental health support, stable jobs, and the benefits they
earned. No veteran should have to struggle through red tape and endless
waits just to get them.

But right now, that’s exactly what’s happening.

In the first year of Donald Trump’s second term, the VA saw its first net
staffing loss in history: more than 40,000 employees, gone. Mental health
services have taken a major hit. Wait times for appointments now average
over 35 days nationwide. Clinical trials for cancer, dementia, and heart
disease face delays.

And with fewer staff left to process claims, veterans face growing
financial instability as benefit-processing bottlenecks leave families
struggling to access the compensation they earned.

True gratitude toward our veterans demands meaningful
action, Peter. At
the Squad Victory Fund, we remain fiercely dedicated to standing with our
veterans, advocating for their rights and protections, and fighting for a
government that shows up for them every single day.

This Veterans Day, let’s honor our veterans, and let’s also hold our
leaders accountable and demand dignity and justice for everyone who
served.

In solidarity,

The Squad Victory Fund

## What the Eight (Dem) Campaigns Reported
Through the **October 14, 2026 reporting cutoff** , the eight campaigns reported approximately:
* **$24.65 million** in total receipts.
* **$21.82 million** in campaign spending.
* **$6.55 million** from other political committees, about **27%** of total receipts.

Political committee contributions include money from corporate-affiliated PACs, labor PACs, trade association PACs, and other political committees.
**OH-1: Greg Landsman**
* Campaign receipts: **$5.66 million**
* Campaign spending: **$5.34 million**
* From other political committees: **$1.20 million**

**OH-3: Joyce Beatty**
* Campaign receipts: **$1.45 million**
* Campaign spending: **$1.43 million**
* From other political committees: **$1.05 million** , about **72%** of receipts

**OH-7: Brian Poindexter**
* Campaign receipts: **$3.72 million**
* Campaign spending: **$2.93 million**
* From other political committees: **$401,000**

**OH-9: Marcy Kaptur**
* Campaign receipts: **$5.91 million**
* Campaign spending: **$5.66 million**
* From other political committees: **$1.51 million** , the highest dollar amount among the eight campaigns

**OH-10: Kristina Knickerbocker**
* Campaign receipts: **$1.02 million**
* Campaign spending: **$882,000**
* From other political committees: **$90,500**

**OH-11: Shontel Brown**
* Campaign receipts: **$1.57 million**
* Campaign spending: **$1.18 million**
* From other political committees: **$984,000** , about **63%** of receipts

**OH-13: Emilia Sykes**
* Campaign receipts: **$3.99 million**
* Campaign spending: **$3.17 million**
* From other political committees: **$1.26 million**

**OH-15: Don Leonard**
* Campaign receipts: **$1.33 million**
* Campaign spending: **$1.23 million**
* From other political committees: **$50,000**

## Outside Spending, District by District
Independent expenditures are separate from campaign receipts and spending. A group can pay for an ad opposing Max Miller without sending any money to Brian Poindexter's campaign.
The lists below show spending **for the Democrat** , **against the Democrat** , and **against the Republican opponent**. They don't include every category of spending in each race. The general election figures for OH-7, OH-9, OH-10, and OH-15 use filings through November 9. The other district totals and some individual spending categories come from the earlier working compilation. Those figures remain provisional until late notices and amendments are reconciled with regular filings.
### OH-1: Greg Landsman
**Outside spending**
* Supporting Landsman: **$1.80 million**
* Opposing Landsman: **$3.61 million**
* Opposing his Republican opponent: **$868,000**

**Selected spending supporting Landsman**
* **CFFE PAC:** About **$643,000**
* **New American Jobs Fund:** About **$507,000**
* **A Strong Innovation Economy Requires Strong IP Protection:** About **$240,000**

**Vendor status:** Specific payees and advertising formats remain unverified.
### OH-3: Joyce Beatty
**Outside spending identified**
* Supporting Beatty: About **$160**
* Opposing Beatty: **None identified** in the records reviewed
* Opposing her Republican opponent: About **$185**

**Groups identified:** Sierra Club Independent Action and Stand Up for Ohio. Direct committee contributions were the larger source of funding in this race.
### OH-7: Brian Poindexter vs. Max Miller
**General election outside spending**
* Supporting Poindexter: About **$740,000**
* Opposing Poindexter: About **$6.8 million**
* Opposing Miller: About **$11.2 million**
* Combined spending supporting Poindexter or opposing Miller: About **$11.9 million**

**Selected general election expenditures**
* **House Majority PAC:** **$6.83 million** in television advertising opposing Miller
* **Your Community PAC:** **$1.98 million** in television advertising opposing Miller
* **Ready for the Fight:** **$1.47 million** in media buys opposing Miller
* **Progressive Turnout Project:** About **$380,000** supporting Poindexter

**Selected primary expenditures, separate from the general election totals**
* **Jobs and Democracy PAC:** About **$570,204** supporting Poindexter in the earlier filing snapshot. That included about **$424,281 for television** and **$70,200 for digital advertising**.
* **BDA PAC:** About **$198,019** supporting Poindexter. The direct-mail vendor remains unconfirmed.

### OH-9: Marcy Kaptur vs. Derek Merrin
**General election outside spending**
* Supporting Kaptur: About **$2.9 million**
* Opposing Kaptur: About **$8.7 million**
* Opposing Merrin: About **$5.5 million**

**Selected spending supporting Kaptur**
* **New American Jobs Fund:** **$695,717** for canvassing
* **AFSCME PEOPLE:** **$584,500** for digital advertising
* **CFFE PAC:** **$527,504** for canvassing
* **AB PAC:** **$365,629** for billboards

**Selected spending opposing Merrin**
* **House Majority PAC:** About **$5.12 million** for television
* **EDW Action Fund:** **$347,351** for digital advertising
* **American Resolve PAC:** About **$60,000** for texting

### OH-10: Kristina Knickerbocker vs. Mike Turner
**General election outside spending**
* Supporting Knickerbocker: About **$1.7 million**
* Opposing Knickerbocker: About **$3.7 million**
* Opposing Turner: About **$6 million**

**Selected spending supporting Knickerbocker**
* **Your Community PAC:** **$804,931** for digital advertising
* **House Majority PAC:** **$287,104** for digital advertising
* **Women Vote:** **$187,859** for digital media
* **Leaders We Deserve:** **$161,670** for digital advertising
* **AB PAC:** **$105,876** for billboards

**Selected spending opposing Turner**
* **House Majority PAC:** About **$4.32 million** for television
* **Your Community PAC:** About **$1.30 million** for television. The filing description also referenced support for Knickerbocker.
* **Innovation Ohio PAC:** About **$235,000** for digital advertising

**Vendor status:** The Ohio agency and media-buyer payments still need to be matched to the original filings.
### OH-11: Shontel Brown
**Outside spending identified**
* Supporting Brown: About **$1,010**
* Opposing Brown: **None identified** in the records reviewed
* Opposing her Republican opponent: About **$185**

**Groups identified:** The Collective Super PAC, Sierra Club Independent Action, and Stand Up for Ohio. As in Beatty's race, direct committee contributions were the larger source of funding.
### OH-13: Emilia Sykes
**Outside spending**
* Supporting Sykes: About **$1.05 million**
* Opposing Sykes: About **$140,000**
* Opposing her Republican opponent: About **$14,000**

**Selected spending supporting Sykes**
* **Think Big PAC:** **$332,071** for digital and streaming advertising
* **New Democrat Majority:** **$270,000** for digital buys and production
* **Rolling Sea Action Fund:** **$230,000** for media production and placement
* **New American Jobs Fund:** **$123,790** for canvassing
* **CFFE PAC:** **$57,790** for canvassing

### OH-15: Don Leonard vs. Mike Carey
**General election outside spending**
* Supporting Leonard: About **$2.5 million**
* Opposing Leonard: About **$2.7 million**
* Opposing Carey: About **$4 million**

**Selected expenditures**
* **Your Community PAC:** About **$1.54 million** supporting Leonard and **$951,000** opposing Carey
* **CFFE PAC:** About **$645,000** supporting Leonard
* **House Majority PAC:** About **$2.5 million** opposing Carey

**Vendor status:** The spending committees are identifiable. The specific Ohio vendor payments still need to be matched to those expenditures.

## Who Funded the Outside Groups?
The amounts below are **national contributions to the committees**. They show who gave to a group that spent money in Ohio. A separate record would be needed to show that a donor's money paid for a particular Ohio ad.
### House Majority PAC
* **House Majority Forward:** About **$93.7 million**. The nonprofit's underlying donors are not fully identified in the PAC's filings.
* **Michael Bloomberg:** **$16 million**
* **Reid Hoffman:** **$8.5 million**
* **Ohio spending identified:** Television opposing Max Miller, Mike Turner, and Derek Merrin, plus spending opposing Mike Carey.

### Your Community PAC
* **American Opportunity Action:** **$10.015 million** in one filing-based compilation. The amount varies across the records reviewed and remains provisional.
* **Sixteen Thirty Fund:** About **$2.74 million**
* **United Futures:** About **$2.58 million**
* **Green Advocacy Project:** **$2 million**
* **Ohio spending identified:** Television opposing Max Miller and Mike Turner, digital advertising supporting Kristina Knickerbocker, and spending supporting Don Leonard and opposing Mike Carey.

### Ready for the Fight
* **JB Pritzker:** About **$10 million** , as identified in the working research.
* **Ohio spending identified:** About **$1.47 million** on media opposing Max Miller.

### Jobs and Democracy PAC
* **Public First Action:** About **$15.4 million** across two reported name variants
* **Public First PAC:** About **$4.05 million**
* **Jan Leike:** **$100,000** in personal contributions
* **Girish Sastry:** **$75,000** in personal contributions
* **Todor Markov:** **$50,000** in personal contributions
* **Ohio spending identified:** About **$570,204** supporting Brian Poindexter in the earlier filing snapshot. The records reviewed do not establish that Anthropic corporate funds paid for those ads.

### Think Big PAC
* **Leading the Future:** **$20 million** across four matched transfers in one filing-based compilation. Think Big reported **$24.5 million** in total political committee receipts. The full amount attributable to Leading the Future still needs reconciliation.
* **Upstream contributors to Leading the Future:** The research identified **a16z Capital Management** and personal contributions from **Greg and Anna Brockman**.
* **Ron Conway:** **$500,000** directly to Think Big
* **Ohio spending identified:** About **$332,071** supporting Emilia Sykes.

### CFFE PAC
* **Pivotal Ventures:** **$2 million**
* **Opportunity Action Fund:** Identified as a contributor, with materially different totals across the compilations reviewed.
* **Ohio spending identified:** Support for Greg Landsman, Marcy Kaptur, Emilia Sykes, and Don Leonard.

### New Democrat Majority
* **Opportunity Forward Alliance:** About **$3.36 million**
* **Effective Governing Coalition:** **$2.25 million**
* **Ohio spending identified:** About **$270,000** for digital advertising and production supporting Emilia Sykes.

## Who Received the Payments?
The committee paying for an ad, the firm it hires, and the station or platform that runs it can be three different entities. Here's what the vendor research identifies so far:
* **Jobs and Democracy PAC -> Bryson Gillette LLC:** About **$19.43 million nationwide**. The national vendor total does not tell us how much the firm received for the Poindexter spending.
* **Think Big PAC -> Lantern Production Consultants LLC:** About **$22.33 million nationwide**. The vendor compilation links Lantern to a roughly **$4,900 media placement fee** supporting Sykes. That fee is part of the **$332,071** in spending supporting her.
* **Think Big PAC -> Manhattan Strategies LLC:** About **$574,000 nationwide**. No Sykes-specific amount is identified here.
* **BDA PAC -> possible Bottled Lightning Collective payment:** The research points to Bottled Lightning as a possible direct-mail vendor for the roughly **$198,000** supporting Poindexter. The original payee record still needs confirmation.

clean_body: Nearly $25 million in campaign receipts, millions more in outside spending, and a district-by-district look at who paid for what. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? We need to find other ANGRY DEMOCRATS. Please consider sharing and subscribing to fuel the ANGER for change. Nearly $25 million in campaign receipts, millions more in outside spending, and a district-by-district look at who paid for what. | | | Nov 11 | | | | | | | | | | | | Hey everyone, this is Matt The Angry Democrat. I want to congratulate everyone who helped Democrats win. I'm excited to see what they can do in Congress. Ohio is sending eight Democrats to Washington after three Republican-held seats flipped and all five Democratic incumbents won reelection. Before we get into it, please consider becoming a paid subscriber to help us produce articles like this throughout the year and hold Congress accountable. I started The Angry Democrat because I believe we have the most say when our own party is in power. That's when we should get off the sidelines, speak directly to the people we elected, and hold them to the promises they made to us. I want healthcare for all, a balanced budget and a lower national debt, a ban on stock trading in Congress and the executive branch, and term limits across all three branches of government. I also want to end corruption, reform campaign finance, and overturn Citizens United. That starts with a record we can come back to: who gave to the campaigns, who spent money independently, and how far we can trace that money. | | ---|---|--- What the Eight (Dem) Campaigns Reported Through the October 14, 2026 reporting cutoff , the eight campaigns reported approximately: $24.65 million in total receipts. $21.82 million in campaign spending. $6.55 million from other political committees, about 27% of total receipts. Political committee contributions include money from corporate-affiliated PACs, labor PACs, trade association PACs, and other political committees. OH-1: Greg Landsman Campaign receipts: $5.66 million Campaign spending: $5.34 million From other political committees: $1.20 million OH-3: Joyce Beatty Campaign receipts: $1.45 million Campaign spending: $1.43 million From other political committees: $1.05 million , about 72% of receipts OH-7: Brian Poindexter Campaign receipts: $3.72 million Campaign spending: $2.93 million From other political committees: $401,000 OH-9: Marcy Kaptur Campaign receipts: $5.91 million Campaign spending: $5.66 million From other political committees: $1.51 million , the highest dollar amount among the eight campaigns OH-10: Kristina Knickerbocker Campaign receipts: $1.02 million Campaign spending: $882,000 From other political committees: $90,500 OH-11: Shontel Brown Campaign receipts: $1.57 million Campaign spending: $1.18 million From other political committees: $984,000 , about 63% of receipts OH-13: Emilia Sykes Campaign receipts: $3.99 million Campaign spending: $3.17 million From other political committees: $1.26 million OH-15: Don Leonard Campaign receipts: $1.33 million Campaign spending: $1.23 million From other political committees: $50,000 Outside Spending, District by District Independent expenditures are separate from campaign receipts and spending. A group can pay for an ad opposing Max Miller without sending any money to Brian Poindexter's campaign. The lists below show spending for the Democrat , against the Democrat , and against the Republican opponent. They don't include every category of spending in each race. The general election figures for OH-7, OH-9, OH-10, and OH-15 use filings through November 9. The other district totals and some individual spending categories come from the earlier working compilation. Those figures remain provisional until late notices and amendments are reconciled with regular filings. OH-1: Greg Landsman Outside spending Supporting Landsman: $1.80 million Opposing Landsman: $3.61 million Opposing his Republican opponent: $868,000 Selected spending supporting Landsman CFFE PAC: About $643,000 New American Jobs Fund: About $507,000 A Strong Innovation Economy Requires Strong IP Protection: About $240,000 Vendor status: Specific payees and advertising formats remain unverified. OH-3: Joyce Beatty Outside spending identified Supporting Beatty: About $160 Opposing Beatty: None identified in the records reviewed Opposing her Republican opponent: About $185 Groups identified: Sierra Club Independent Action and Stand Up for Ohio. Direct committee contributions were the larger source of funding in this race. OH-7: Brian Poindexter vs. Max Miller General election outside spending Supporting Poindexter: About $740,000 Opposing Poindexter: About $6.8 million Opposing Miller: About $11.2 million Combined spending supporting Poindexter or opposing Miller: About $11.9 million Selected general election expenditures House Majority PAC: $6.83 million in television advertising opposing Miller Your Community PAC: $1.98 million in television advertising opposing Miller Ready for the Fight: $1.47 million in media buys opposing Miller Progressive Turnout Project: About $380,000 supporting Poindexter Selected primary expenditures, separate from the general election totals Jobs and Democracy PAC: About $570,204 supporting Poindexter in the earlier filing snapshot. That included about $424,281 for television and $70,200 for digital advertising. BDA PAC: About $198,019 supporting Poindexter. The direct-mail vendor remains unconfirmed. OH-9: Marcy Kaptur vs. Derek Merrin General election outside spending Supporting Kaptur: About $2.9 million Opposing Kaptur: About $8.7 million Opposing Merrin: About $5.5 million Selected spending supporting Kaptur New American Jobs Fund: $695,717 for canvassing AFSCME PEOPLE: $584,500 for digital advertising CFFE PAC: $527,504 for canvassing AB PAC: $365,629 for billboards Selected spending opposing Merrin House Majority PAC: About $5.12 million for television EDW Action Fund: $347,351 for digital advertising American Resolve PAC: About $60,000 for texting OH-10: Kristina Knickerbocker vs. Mike Turner General election outside spending Supporting Knickerbocker: About $1.7 million Opposing Knickerbocker: About $3.7 million Opposing Turner: About $6 million Selected spending supporting Knickerbocker Your Community PAC: $804,931 for digital advertising House Majority PAC: $287,104 for digital advertising Women Vote: $187,859 for digital media Leaders We Deserve: $161,670 for digital advertising AB PAC: $105,876 for billboards Selected spending opposing Turner House Majority PAC: About $4.32 million for television Your Community PAC: About $1.30 million for television. The filing description also referenced support for Knickerbocker. Innovation Ohio PAC: About $235,000 for digital advertising Vendor status: The Ohio agency and media-buyer payments still need to be matched to the original filings. OH-11: Shontel Brown Outside spending identified Supporting Brown: About $1,010 Opposing Brown: None identified in the records reviewed Opposing her Republican opponent: About $185 Groups identified: The Collective Super PAC, Sierra Club Independent Action, and Stand Up for Ohio. As in Beatty's race, direct committee contributions were the larger source of funding. OH-13: Emilia Sykes Outside spending Supporting Sykes: About $1.05 million Opposing Sykes: About $140,000 Opposing her Republican opponent: About $14,000 Selected spending supporting Sykes Think Big PAC: $332,071 for digital and streaming advertising New Democrat Majority: $270,000 for digital buys and production Rolling Sea Action Fund: $230,000 for media production and placement New American Jobs Fund: $123,790 for canvassing CFFE PAC: $57,790 for canvassing OH-15: Don Leonard vs. Mike Carey General election outside spending Supporting Leonard: About $2.5 million Opposing Leonard: About $2.7 million Opposing Carey: About $4 million Selected expenditures Your Community PAC: About $1.54 million supporting Leonard and $951,000 opposing Carey CFFE PAC: About $645,000 supporting Leonard House Majority PAC: About $2.5 million opposing Carey Vendor status: The spending committees are identifiable. The specific Ohio vendor payments still need to be matched to those expenditures. Who Funded the Outside Groups? The amounts below are national contributions to the committees. They show who gave to a group that spent money in Ohio. A separate record would be needed to show that a donor's money paid for a particular Ohio ad. House Majority PAC House Majority Forward: About $93.7 million. The nonprofit's underlying donors are not fully identified in the PAC's filings. Michael Bloomberg: $16 million Reid Hoffman: $8.5 million Ohio spending identified: Television opposing Max Miller, Mike Turner, and Derek Merrin, plus spending opposing Mike Carey. Your Community PAC American Opportunity Action: $10.015 million in one filing-based compilation. The amount varies across the records reviewed and remains provisional. Sixteen Thirty Fund: About $2.74 million United Futures: About $2.58 million Green Advocacy Project: $2 million Ohio spending identified: Television opposing Max Miller and Mike Turner, digital advertising supporting Kristina Knickerbocker, and spending supporting Don Leonard and opposing Mike Carey. Ready for the Fight JB Pritzker: About $10 million , as identified in the working research. Ohio spending identified: About $1.47 million on media opposing Max Miller. Jobs and Democracy PAC Public First Action: About $15.4 million across two reported name variants Public First PAC: About $4.05 million Jan Leike: $100,000 in personal contributions Girish Sastry: $75,000 in personal contributions Todor Markov: $50,000 in personal contributions Ohio spending identified: About $570,204 supporting Brian Poindexter in the earlier filing snapshot. The records reviewed do not establish that Anthropic corporate funds paid for those ads. Think Big PAC Leading the Future: $20 million across four matched transfers in one filing-based compilation. Think Big reported $24.5 million in total political committee receipts. The full amount attributable to Leading the Future still needs reconciliation. Upstream contributors to Leading the Future: The research identified a16z Capital Management and personal contributions from Greg and Anna Brockman. Ron Conway: $500,000 directly to Think Big Ohio spending identified: About $332,071 supporting Emilia Sykes. CFFE PAC Pivotal Ventures: $2 million Opportunity Action Fund: Identified as a contributor, with materially different totals across the compilations reviewed. Ohio spending identified: Support for Greg Landsman, Marcy Kaptur, Emilia Sykes, and Don Leonard. New Democrat Majority Opportunity Forward Alliance: About $3.36 million Effective Governing Coalition: $2.25 million Ohio spending identified: About $270,000 for digital advertising and production supporting Emilia Sykes. Who Received the Payments? The committee paying for an ad, the firm it hires, and the station or platform that runs it can be three different entities. Here's what the vendor research identifies so far: Jobs and Democracy PAC -> Bryson Gillette LLC: About $19.43 million nationwide. The national vendor total does not tell us how much the firm received for the Poindexter spending. Think Big PAC -> Lantern Production Consultants LLC: About $22.33 million nationwide. The vendor compilation links Lantern to a roughly $4,900 media placement fee supporting Sykes. That fee is part of the $332,071 in spending supporting her. Think Big PAC -> Manhattan Strategies LLC: About $574,000 nationwide. No Sykes-specific amount is identified here. BDA PAC -> possible Bottled Lightning Collective payment: The research points to Bottled Lightning as a possible direct-mail vendor for the roughly $198,000 supporting Poindexter. The original payee record still needs confirmation. Who Gave Directly to the Campaigns? These are selected contributions from the working compilation. Each amount is approximate. Joyce Beatty Huntington Bancshares PAC: $10,000 Fifth Third PAC: $10,000 Goldman Sachs PAC: $10,000 Regions Financial PAC: $10,000 FICO PAC: $10,000 American Electric Power political committee: $10,000 Marcy Kaptur Honeywell PAC: $10,000 Emilia Sykes Honeywell PAC: $10,000 Huntington Bancshares PAC: $5,000 Shontel Brown TransDigm Group employee PAC: $10,000 to Brown's campaign Hy-Vee Employees PAC: $10,000 Zurich Holding Company of America PAC: $10,000 Rock Holdings PAC: $10,000 Separate leadership PAC contribution: TransDigm's PAC also gave about $10,000 to Strength in Seven , Brown's affiliated leadership PAC. Selected individual contributions grouped by reported employer Greg Landsman: About $18,000 from individuals listing Kroger as their employer. Shontel Brown: About $14,000 from individuals listing TransDigm Group as their employer. Emilia Sykes: About $11,000 from individuals listing Summa Health as their employer. Stay Angry. # Wednesday, November 11, 2026

**Good Morning!** On this day in 1921, an unknown American soldier killed in World War I was laid to rest at [_Arlington National Cemetery_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkD1upTAURldjOhA2hvcoXEwxdG-aSZQSXdvXcBX_IONA2H30kiXkW8B3dM7bY34AeYrLPwioyuHmiOfusRTMc9owXukj44W7gbABLdFpSm4WrRhqzmvOZzCFDpwlVFY5kAhjhYrfRtmNfd931aokSK5Na40Zhe617loQ2lhptO1QuKEi9fzjPxMdb_BmcbzrO-8HuPMBmWzRUkm5KSselBeKBM5f6cDcmBQqr9ZStp11f5iYmJjO82wgP71KigYDFsxXE8gzMf393HzKyMT0koKuk6vLivVrfI_pjPX_5C1hrrKy20ne0z7cmGyXAOS_UeWXlQ4lvgIAAP__Wkh_vA). President Warren G. Harding presided over the Armistice Day ceremony. Happy Veterans Day to those of you who served our country, and thank you for your service! See [_yesterday’s edition_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDFvgzAQhX8NbEScjbEZPHTJlq4d0RGfyUnGRsZxxL-v0q7d-tb39D3p-7rNN-TAcf3EjWypfo70OgKVQnlOO8UzPTOddNxx25HX6BdOfha9GDuADmDGe-FK84Ctsx4HwqklC3oa5KSUku3Dil5rY5T0o1rASCFJG1ADodNTT0a1bN88-I2QcCHtaDKLATWigZGaoSfHJeVLeVDlvHJk9OFMlfLlnrY22Ecp-9HIj0ZcG3H9e_YunnQ4PLuYKm0L5Q767n3eiGubrdtfHAIfo26Gft2Qww-9_FNMteI7AAD__7dBd9I) for a roundup of restaurants offering free meals to veterans today, and check out _Et Cetera_ below for a statewide roundup of ceremonies honoring your service. Think about everything you do for your car. The oil changes, the premium gas, and the long warm-up on frosty mornings. Some of those habits keep you safe, and some just keep the service bay busy. ## DMV Launches ‘Open Your Eyes’ Campaign
The Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles has [_launched a statewide campaign_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0DuO6zAMBdDV2B0DSf4XKl7jLq-d0mAs2iEgfyBxZGT3A02QFQw7gsDFPfy6T3dkz_v6HzeykpZppyt6EqEwHSftr-M70IvijNuJvO7Lg49lMsq0oDVoPeEsnGiqsXR2wZpwKMnqbqiroWmaqnzavu6WoTNoGlJKDY3rjFNaqRo7fBBVJducp99jKn2jztHQP3rdtNjrlopakWM5wk2elDisvDMu_nUkCrf52EpvnyJnLKp_hRkLM16RJB8KM2ZPYUZ_zOjfK3wSwG0JMhKyEjITPk4QDCtJBMdRAs5CDlzgxPsKUVDoYkfAO-TqZbDuvNh7jm1X1GrdkP1vMfnjT5M1PwEAAP__4zSOtA) called “Open Your Eyes” that compares glancing at your phone behind the wheel to driving with your eyes shut. The centerpiece television ad shows two distracted drivers covering their faces with their hands, then freezes time an instant before they collide. It began rolling out this month across broadcast, streaming, and digital services. So far in 2026, Virginia State Police data show [_11,953 crashes_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LvO3CAQBeCnwR0rg_GtoEjjbtOmtGZhsEfCF8HYq337iET7BP_Uo6Nzvj_P-QkUaV9-w4aW7zDv-M4RmTHNx4n757gSfjA72E6gZQ8vOsKsa91JpaRSMzimG2cDlbcBDMJYoVX9aJqxbdumWi0MXoNRvnPB904NvglD0zvTvsJYj8ZVZEue-n-6UQ_sPY7Da1BtB4PqUJgaPfGRHrziTWmhnSDEz3Fjerhjq6Jdmc8sml9CT0JPcC1XZggJ8UyYc3kSeirbhJ6-CdJvt4xw7W7FLGFnkp4yJ3CMXvpENyb5HS55BZbEWTqIRUwWHll8ZAESeqqS9eebYqTc9cLUywYU__XjH9LeVv8NAAD__7tFk0o), 93 deaths, and 816 serious injuries involving a distracted driver. About 10% of those drivers were distracted by cellphone use or texting. The campaign was developed to “shift the mindset of those who see no harm in taking their eyes off the road,” said DMV Commissioner Saundra Jack, the Governor’s Highway Safety Representative.
## Lawmakers Weigh Tougher Plate-Reader Rules
A Virginia State Crime Commission report found seven police [_agencies reported keeping license-plate reader data_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OrSAUhZ9GOw0giBYUt7E7t52SbGCjO8GfQY7mvP3kzGSeYFb9rbWS7-NhH0CJtvk_rGjKFe2G95mwFMx2P3B77c-MLzw9rAfQvEVHe7SCib7hvOHcgi90oZVQBxNBIow1Gq5H2Y1Kqa5ejGMxdhC1F9rB6Mage6dQ9jLwKLQaajLvPf4T0fEWdcBxcANXPQy8x0oyDFT23JYFL8ozbQQxvfYLc-v3tU5mKeU4q-5fJaZKTPd9v1GPW8F8fj4h45urxPTbrsQEuZBPaLWEIDmDhjPmGxmdagCFarrBMY8AvB98u5Q11dmE46aU6Ox1Jdm8AqXv__JHdZcRXwEAAP__GzWDhA) longer than the state’s 21-day limit, including one that held mobile-camera data for 90 days. That’s down from 33 in the commission’s January report. Of the 351 agencies that responded to the survey, 191 said they use the cameras. Most reported complying, though six lacked a required policy and a few improperly shared data with federal or out-of-state agencies. Twenty agencies reported unauthorized use by employees, and seven criminal charges had been filed in two Virginia general district courts as of October, all still pending. Hampton Commonwealth’s Attorney Anton Bell, a commission member, said the cameras have clear benefits but need “checks and balances.” Richmond and Henrico have already [_moved to end their camera contracts_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2upSAQx58GO8wBFLGg2MbubLulGXHwTIJgkMWct9949t4nuFNMMpnk9__485yfQIHi9ht2tKX6OeJ1BiwF85wOjO_0N-MbTwf7AbRFv1Dys3xIzYXgQszgClWcO2hW66FDGBu0Yhg7NfZ9r5qX1RqN8cYPWivUizIKEZQzA4Jbh8U3ZG-e-D9SiRaHFUezGNFrMEIj6x64Ukm5LS-slDeKBD68U8XcurQ3wb5KOU6mfjE5MTld19VepX6eTE53JiankBwE_nV8Y_iRAjnk94on8iNAQZ4RVswnj6nykd_2mmzX46IQ6NQD6x7bDhQ-4uWHvVUr_wUAAP__m4mEqA). The centerpiece television ad shows two distracted drivers covering their faces with their hands, then freezes time an instant before they collide. It began rolling out this month across broadcast, streaming, and digital services. So far in 2026, Virginia State Police data show , 93 deaths, and 816 serious injuries involving a distracted driver. About 10% of those drivers were distracted by cellphone use or texting. The campaign was developed to “shift the mindset of those who see no harm in taking their eyes off the road,” said DMV Commissioner Saundra Jack, the Governor’s Highway Safety Representative. Lawmakers Weigh Tougher Plate-Reader Rules A Virginia State Crime Commission report found seven police longer than the state’s 21-day limit, including one that held mobile-camera data for 90 days. That’s down from 33 in the commission’s January report. Of the 351 agencies that responded to the survey, 191 said they use the cameras. Most reported complying, though six lacked a required policy and a few improperly shared data with federal or out-of-state agencies. Twenty agencies reported unauthorized use by employees, and seven criminal charges had been filed in two Virginia general district courts as of October, all still pending. Hampton Commonwealth’s Attorney Anton Bell, a commission member, said the cameras have clear benefits but need “checks and balances.” Richmond and Henrico have already . **Good Morning!** On this day in 1918, the guns of World War I fell silent at the [eleventh hour](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOtCAUhZ8GO81wIagFxd_Yzd9uae7AVdkgGLjR-PabmXLbPe1JzvnyfT3nJ4YY0vofd7K85DnRVSMxU5mXUCrXlK9E15qPSOipYPI4wwNMK2Ur5YyOw0mzbLxdiIBUQ1b2o1aj6aVuNvtC5wZFSjtvln5QygA6Y3wPTvnxhU2w7zn5iZLadM6PqAgB5KBBDaPQD_KBc-m-c0i80RLvfFLpXN6baDfmowr1T8AkYPJ0YOGdEncndms-BUwn8Ru8th5vAdMWKudyt3lpfzVNsf64Qoyhml7ox7pjiJ8b_puc08JPAAAA__9hY3qn) of the eleventh day of the eleventh month. ## First Snow of the Season Is on the Way

clean_body: The first snowflakes of the season are expected late this week in the interior Northeast, with , Vermont, and New Hampshire most likely to see them as a nor'easter moves up the coast. | | | | | | Wednesday, November 11, 2026 ---|--- Good Morning! On this day in 1918, the guns of World War I fell silent at the of the eleventh day of the eleventh month. Congress renamed Armistice Day as Veterans Day in 1954 to honor Americans who served in every war. Happy Veterans Day. To everyone who wore the uniform, and to the families who waited at home, thank you. This country is what it is because of you. If you served, or someone you love did, reply and tell us which branch. We'd love to hear your story. Think about everything you do for your car. The oil changes, the premium gas, and the long warm-up on frosty mornings. Some of those habits keep you safe, and some just keep the service bay busy. Today we're counting down the five car habits that truly protect you, and the five that only drain your wallet. One of them costs American drivers more than $2 billion a year. So which side is your routine on? All of that and more on The Flyover Podcast. ! Today's sponsor, , explores the hormonal changes behind thinning hair after 50 and shares a menopause specialist's approach to supporting fuller-looking hair. | First Snow of the Season Is on the Way The are expected late this week in the interior Northeast, with upstate New York, Vermont, and New Hampshire most likely to see them as a storm system moves toward the Northeast. The big cities get a soaking instead. Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, and Washington are in line for a cold, windy rain, heaviest into Friday morning, with street flooding possible in New York. Mountain roads from West Virginia to the Adirondacks could turn slick. Then comes the cold, starting today. Temperatures will run 20 to 25 degrees below normal from the Canadian border to the Gulf Coast, with wind chills near freezing in Chicago and Atlanta and a , cold enough to kill unprotected plants, in parts of the South. It won't last. Forecasters expect to return to the East next week. name: Wes Moore
subject: Veterans Day
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=2293%2E1086043%2E0Wzob_)
Peter,
Happy Veterans Day to all the veterans who have served in Maryland and across the country.
**As a former service member, I am proud to support our veterans.**
[](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261111-1.7nw-zR&refcode=em-20261111-1&t=2&akid=2293%2E1086043%2E0Wzob_)
Maryland has a long and proud military tradition, unmatched by any other state. Today, more than 335,000 Veterans call Maryland home, and they play a critical role in our state and economy.
We've helped house veterans and their families who have nowhere to go, lowered health and dental care costs for our Guard members, supported veterans and military families during the longest federal shutdown in our country’s history, turned our state’s veterans home from one star to four, and helped military spouses get hired and keep working when they move here.
But there is so much more we need to do to support our military community. We need to make sure that "thank you for your service" is more than just a quote, or something that we always put at the end of a sentence.
We can and must do more as a state for the men and women who have worn the uniform of our country and sacrificed so much to keep us safe and protect our freedoms.
Just like they have fought for us on the frontlines, I will continue to fight for them.
Elevate,
Wes

| | Friend, Today on Veterans Day, we take a moment to honor the courageous men and women who stepped forward to wear our nation’s uniform and fight for our freedoms and our nation. As the daughter and granddaughter of Army, Navy, and Air Force veterans, this day is personal — and I treat my role on the Armed Services Committee as an extension of my deepest gratitude to those who serve. 50,000 veterans, active-duty service members, and military families call Maryland’s Third District home. I’ve made it my mission to ensure that promises made to our military personnel are kept. That’s why I’ve spent my first term in Congress fighting to fund mental health services and expand access to high-quality care at military medical facilities like Walter Reed. To every veteran and military family across our communities, our state, and our nation: Thank you for your service, your sacrifice, and your steadfast commitment to our nation. We are forever grateful. _To our veterans: If you or a fellow veteran needs assistance with the VA or any other federal agency, my office is always here to help._ Warmly, Sarah Elfreth

## Tyler Man Charged in Cruise Killing
A 48-year-old Tyler man told FBI agents he [struck and choked his wife](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL3O3SAMhq-GbERg-EgYGLpk-7p2jBxwEnTIj4CTnN59lfYS6s2y9ep9nl_f4zfGFPflJ27k6mc-xp3ukqhWyiPmTKXG3ed3LPSK6fmsx7mMIMBwKbmUI_oaLxplE9wkgpUNOdlZrWyvrWpWh4hGGRMC-U4r8nrSXirbqzB5azvVRPekyWdASKVaKbD3ggJQhzMFybSgEOuR27pSpQ-WOf0-LsqtP7YmubXWszD1g8HAYLjvu32tx_s5Mhgw1-gTMRgeMAaDz3F71q14XgiLx5P49s6BMl8wXVTqsfN_yLys8WQwQP_FhZ1DAPvFjZaG6wATn8wMPICQfvYABmWTXTjvx1MxHdNi2TCmvy3rf8q9HPwJAAD__w23jm4) in their cabin aboard the _MSC Seascape_ on Sunday, hours after the ship left Galveston, court documents state. Jason Watford said an argument over dinner with his wife, Susan, made him "snap," and he choked her. The couple's child was in the cabin and is now [safe in foster care](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFyhCAQhp9GOxwWPTwLijR2lzalg7AoExQH9vTy9hkuj5Ctv_3n_7-vx_TQPvh9-dQbKnq5OO145YBEmCadEmbyu0lPn_Hbh0JSPJZJcCEZAAOYtCF_4gS1VTO3A9SooB-6drh3Q1uvau61me_GWmek7ME6tGaWww1ug3T81tVelTQoJzi0bQNc3w1HK7DXDi1UHUfrKaaGViR86ezCTzwxNSZudVAr0ZGr9qMSYyXG67oaF19CrvGZKe4FqsRYZlVifL-zTe_MrDotaNn2TBYTW3Q4sfAs7nPUybItG_a3nOXVHwwAeGlaJ2WPq8jIsq86vmzah3cV-qfBU4nfAAAA__9_GIj1), the state said. Watford pleaded guilty in 2024 to [assaulting his wife](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFywyAMhp_G3sghwNgMDF2ypWtHHwYRcyWxD1Qnffsead-g2nSSvtP3f1zmi0s53a_v7oaWnnGb7_ioGYmwzK4UrJTuvnylip8pt03a9ussuNAMgAHMzlM6cIY-2IUHAz1aGI2SZlJG9qt1ykcZtJ4m7QFjWEBFPagxCsGjlqJPttGgleAg5Qm4mzzHIHB0EQN0imNItJUTrUj4dDXm7-3AcvLbrc92JdprJ986ce7E2e3NoI1aUyj5jJ04_zqwuqad_ZmwF4vFJbGKrnq3IxuHiAtXMA1-4VxrB0ZGowyfgvHDIvpiw_5o91WPneLXm0v59Qf9M77Dip8AAAD__99OhKo) after she told a Smith County officer he grabbed her wrist during an argument over money. He got 15 months of probation, court records show. A housekeeper delivering towels saw [blood on his hands](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHSpCAQhJ8GMywGFJeA4BKzvfRCi4VRqUOxYFb33v7K_3-Ef8Lpru76-s9zerqY4r78dhta-sx52vGqCYmwTK4UrBR3X96x4t-YbiflY5mkkJoDcIDJeYonTtAE-xLBQIMWBtMp8-iMalbb6_BSITiEHoJW_esxGGW80UEYjaZvor3T4D4pQKkWhHt4gUHi4GYMwDqBIVIuLa1I-HF1Tv_yiaX1eWuSXYmOytQvJkcmx-u6Wr-WvN8qk-PyTjP32VVicnSFok94v106sVLe-Tcdr2s8-PYuAQvfqudS9lIa0O2xHk2x4bhu_qoH1ollczF9tdMPRzut_B8AAP__VQKC2w) and Susan motionless on the floor. Watford is on a federal hold in the Galveston County Jail and faces up to life in prison if convicted.
## Hinojosa Rate Freeze Faces Legal Doubts
Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa, a Democrat, plans to declare a "high-cost emergency" within an hour of being sworn in on Jan. 19 and [freeze residential electricity rates](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGS4yAMhp_G7vAA9iVQUFzjLtde6VGwsDVLjBeUONmn3yH7CKtS0qfR__2_TBegSNvyD27o-BnStOFRIjJjniBnLEybz3cq-EGxbnLal0lLfRJKCaUm8EwPnFQ7u6ucrWrRqbMdemsG27erO1kLRmplrfHGW381g4beBPyD6IPFlly9pmppqfq-UxKMlzhrPEPAWTWDxJk45Y5XZHxCCfGVHpg7n25tdCvzXpr-b6PHRo_HcXQhPWuMOm_0uKdITL40enzTYqnwlrLAiJ7FHmETISN-4U8nkyd-iT2TxyIyUMEiPu_VRdqKiLhAFHDnNWXiV5vdvB9VTjmdm0EuN6D4fo1_afTh9HcAAAD__xgwkWk) by executive order. Hinojosa says the freeze answers what she calls an affordability crisis and is part of a push to make corporations "finally pay their fair share." Since 2002, most Texans have shopped among more than 100 competing electricity providers. Nick Loris, president of the free-market group C3 Solutions, expects providers to [challenge the emergency in court](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGS4yAMQL8Gd3gAO3ZcUFzjLtde6VFAtnUhkAFtnOzX75BfWLV686R5_y7LBShQ3P7CHS2_1rREPEpAZswL5IyFKbr8RQVvFCrJ6bEtRplBai21XsAxPXHRjbdX5SfdoNXj1HfTuZ-6ZrfeAKA-D4MzEwzXfjxNpwqcvEFvBt-QrTZdxyjdda1WcHYKvcERVvRa9Ao9ccot78j4grKGd3pibl26N8HuzI8iuj_CzMLMx3G0Ny5Ql8LMO8X0PxWQB0QukpNcM-I3yo9IYkDHmRzxW2ZgLDJFuVIuLD28JRS51UsxZWHmJlv_OGqGMoyiV9sdKHye4F-2e1rzEwAA___k2Ydi) and doubts rising prices qualify as a disaster under state law. He warned a freeze could leave providers unable to cover costs, threatening supply. The Public Utility Commission regulates key parts of the market. Making data centers pay more for the grid [may require lawmakers to act](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4zAMRL9G7hiIsh3HhYtr3O21VxqKRNtCFNGQmDj79wftLywrghjwzcy_r-XLhhjS9tc-aZLPykuis0QSobzYnKlISC6_QqFHiFUpfGyL0eYKiIC4WCfhTQs2frprP2JDEw5j1463bmybfboO2JFfO-pJ9-NtbO-rbnscVtvjtfe3Jkz1G9YxGtv2gtrenCZvaLAreVSdJh-E80V2EvrYssZvflO-OH42cdpFjqLaP8rMyszneV5cDO5hdn4V4VRVysw1lzJzZGejMnNlKjMjKjPruslO4LgI8AoPoiOkDeothm2XApzg3K3ADx8SfQS26iFxBsev6MEzCEPkkzJQJCc5uCDfcA8xVnKTJ3-ctcRyHVSnt6cN8SeC_LL592T-BwAA__-4fZrR).
## Cruz Opens GOP Base in Austin
Sen. Ted Cruz is [opening an Austin headquarters](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1u7CAQhZ8Gd6yYgetdFxS3cbdpU1oExgYFGwdmf5Knj7yvkNOeo0_6zvt1urqU07a8uZUsP-cybfRomZipTq5Wapw2X2-p0WfKx5LLvkyosJcAEmByntOdJuiC_VBhgI4snAejh4sZdBetDsGght4Nc_Bae-hhCP4SZhM0mn_YJXvQ4Agq0PoEyl28ooB0djMFEEZRSFzqiSMxPV2b83e5Uz35snbZRua9Cf1f4Chw5Egx5Xx0AsdYVjqMBI7erbtLyyZw7BGg10YyBenr7Udmd9t8pCZfeLmUXcYvgWNXbdgfh3jrz8KoZXXphe74j2_dLf4GAAD__2pXf8s) for Saving Texas, a nonprofit run by his allies, to recruit Republican candidates and rebuild the party's grassroots network after last week's GOP losses. In the United States under Trump, there are few spectacles more gratifying these days than the sight of MAGA lawmakers--including GOP Speaker Mike Johnson-- discovering the country has grown tired of them.
The spectacle has now been made even sweeter with the Democratic victors arriving in Washington, D.C. smiling, energetic, and possessed with the notion that government might actually be conducted in the public interest.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0b12773d-842a-49d6-8481-6f3e1d4c972d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This was the pleasing scene on Capitol Hill as the newly elected Democratic senators and representatives arrived for their orientation meetings. They came carrying their luggage, their hopes, their briefing books, and perhaps a modest supply of aspirin for the headaches that accompany the discovery of how Washington works. The new arrivals looked cheerful, purposeful, positively delighted to be there.
What a wonderful sight.
After years of watching the Republican Party turn Congress into a combination of sleazy traveling circus, Ayn Rand debating society, and badly managed lunatic asylum, the appearance of these new Democrats was like opening the curtains in a room that has been occupied too long by unwashed meth addicts.
You could practically hear the furniture sigh with relief.

That's why I created the brand-new _**[2027 Pathway to Victory Daily Devotional](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckb2K3TAQhZ9G7mysn2vZhYoEx5BiA2GLLcWsNPYO2JKQZIf79sFk9wUy7TnfwMd5e7EvQDuF7RccaKgUm4t9xjNTuKhCpRhqhCdCjmtJVvRiaDlvObfgKl1oFTTePAQf17FBw_Wk5DRJOTYfBpTQahwUer16r7XS_aCUkxreJ_Xo-4bM_Y_fJ_hDPrpxfB-c8F6tCAOfOFP9mTxU7CgU8lhcjCnFnSq50sW8Nbv5qDUVJr8xsTCxFHRnxi7V646ZWEQvdJvq5X27bZzJpcQzO7QuemRyfvvxnYnhrId1cCSgLTA5e6D9aT1e8faH_bPxj2RyTjmWhK5S2D6jAz2dB5MzHkBffRdDxVCZnH_r9ufra_tl22Tj0x_adyqDZqrfbqhz8Wjqf05wGfE3AAD__yBXmCM),**_ a weekday guide to help you start each day with biblical truth and encouragement. Every devotional in this 260-entry collection was written to help you think biblically, live obediently, and trust God more fully. Whether you're struggling with uncertainty, carrying the weight of past mistakes, or simply seeking God's direction, this resource is designed to meet you right where you are. You'll begin the year by discovering how to embrace the new beginning God offers. You'll turn your attention to Jesus Christ through Holy Week and a study of the end times. You'll follow the early church and see how the Holy Spirit empowered believers to stand firm in their faith. And you'll close the year examining the attitudes that shape your life, learning to find contentment and experiencing the freedom of forgiveness. These are not abstract ideas. They are time-tested truths drawn from over four decades of biblical teaching to help you walk closely with Christ each day. name: Molly Gray
subject: Honoring Our Veterans
body:
Dear Peter, Today, on Veterans Day, we honor the brave men and women who have served our country, as well as the families who have stood beside them. Their courage, sacrifice, and commitment to something greater than themselves represent the very best of our nation. We owe our veterans more than our gratitude. We owe them a commitment to ensuring they and their families have access to the care, support, and opportunities they have earned. That commitment is personal to me and my husband, Mike. My dad was a Marine First Lieutenant, and my brother a Marine Corporal who enlisted and served in Iraq. Mike’s father served in the Vietnam War as a Staff Sergeant with the 555th Fighter Squadron (“Triple Nickel”) out of Udorn Air Force Base. Sadly, Nick passed away unexpectedly in June. We are thinking of Nick today, as well as family and friends who have served on active duty, and all those veterans across Vermont and our nation who have sacrificed so much. This morning, I’ll be heading to Montpelier for a Veteran’s Day gathering. Below, I’ve shared some events happening today across Vermont. I encourage you, if you can, to attend an event near your, or find a way that feels meaningful to honor and thank the veterans in your life and community. Very Respectfully, _Molly Gray_
_**Wednesday, November 11 | Veterans Day**_ **Stowe | 8:30 a.m. and 11:00 a.m.**
Enjoy a free Veterans Day breakfast at Stowe Middle/High School at 8:30 a.m., followed by a service at 11:00 a.m. in front of the Akeley Memorial Building. **Williston | 9:00–10:00 a.m.**
The Williston-Richmond Rotary Club will host a Veterans Day observance at Williston War Memorial Park.[ Event details](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143260433/659634515/1927184913?CalendarItemId=b001a32d-6312-4ea4-acb0-bd39070f89d4&Start=2026-11-11&End=2026-11-11&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyNTNjNTc5ZS1jYmRkLWYxMTEtOTFmNS0wMDIyNDgyNGQ5ZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Eum0oxP3CRwpCKk_yozEfiOmBYDFU8sXIm0xnZLoESU=&emci=e6cdb104-6add-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&emdi=253c579e-cbdd-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&ceid=43402276) **Barre | 10:00 a.m. and 11:00 a.m.**
A Veterans Day parade will begin at Barre Auditorium at 10:00 a.m., followed by a ceremony at Barre City Park at 11:00 a.m. **Bennington | 11:00 a.m.**
The Veterans Day parade will begin at 11:00 a.m., traveling from Scott Street east toward Safford Street. Parade participants will line up beginning at 10:00 a.m. [Event details](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143260434/659634516/-323529574?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyNTNjNTc5ZS1jYmRkLWYxMTEtOTFmNS0wMDIyNDgyNGQ5ZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Eum0oxP3CRwpCKk_yozEfiOmBYDFU8sXIm0xnZLoESU=&emci=e6cdb104-6add-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&emdi=253c579e-cbdd-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&ceid=43402276) **St. Albans | 10:30 a.m. and 11:00 a.m.**
A Veterans Day parade will depart from Bellows Free Academy at 10:30 a.m., followed by a ceremony in Taylor Park at 11:00 a.m. VFW Post 758 will also serve free soup and sandwiches from 2:00–4:00 p.m. **South Royalton | 10:15 a.m.–2:00 p.m.**
Vermont Law and Graduate School will host its annual Veterans Day program at the Chase Community Center, with a livestream available for those unable to attend in person. [Program details and livestream](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143260435/659634517/-1825857149?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyNTNjNTc5ZS1jYmRkLWYxMTEtOTFmNS0wMDIyNDgyNGQ5ZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Eum0oxP3CRwpCKk_yozEfiOmBYDFU8sXIm0xnZLoESU=&emci=e6cdb104-6add-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&emdi=253c579e-cbdd-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&ceid=43402276) **Montpelier | 11:00 a.m.**
A Veterans Day wreath-laying ceremony will take place at Montpelier High School, followed by an open house and luncheon at VFW Post 792 at noon. [Event details](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143260436/659634518/1178897997?_evDiscoveryPath=/event/3887282-montpelier-veterans-day-ceremony&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyNTNjNTc5ZS1jYmRkLWYxMTEtOTFmNS0wMDIyNDgyNGQ5ZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Eum0oxP3CRwpCKk_yozEfiOmBYDFU8sXIm0xnZLoESU=&emci=e6cdb104-6add-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&emdi=253c579e-cbdd-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&ceid=43402276) **Pittsford | 11:00 a.m.**
A Veterans Day ceremony will be held at the Pittsford Town Offices. **Brattleboro | 11:00 a.m.**
VFW Post 1034 will host a ceremony featuring guest speaker Michelle LeBlanc, a retired veteran and state trooper, along with performances by the Post 5 American Legion Band. **Burlington | 11:00 a.m.**
Join the city for its annual Veterans Day Commemoration at Battery Park. **Rutland | 11:00 a.m.**
The community will gather at Main Street Memorial Park for a World War II memorial unveiling, followed by lunch at Rutland American Legion Post 31. **Milton and Colchester | 10:00 a.m. and 12:00 p.m.**
The Colchester-Milton Rotary Club's annual Flags for Heroes project will display American flags throughout both communities. Celebrations will take place at 10:00 a.m. inside the R.R. Charlebois, Inc. truck showroom and at noon at the Colchester Recreation Center. **Northfield | 4:15 p.m.**
Norwich University will host a special Veterans Day ceremony featuring keynote speaker Major General Gary W. Keefe, Norwich alumnus and 43rd Adjutant General of the Massachusetts National Guard. Burlington | 11:00 a.m. Join the city for its annual Veterans Day Commemoration at Battery Park. Rutland | 11:00 a.m. The community will gather at Main Street Memorial Park for a World War II memorial unveiling, followed by lunch at Rutland American Legion Post 31. body:

Hi Friend,
Today we honor the men and women who put on the uniform and gave their time, their strength, and sometimes everything they had to protect our freedom.
[](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)
| | | __ As an Air Force veteran, I know that service reaches far beyond the person in uniform. It reaches the spouses who held down the home front, the children who waited for a parent to return, and the families who carry the cost long after the mission ends.
Over the past year, I met veterans in every corner of this district. Their stories reminded me why this country is worth defending.
If you or someone you love has served, thank you. Our freedom exists because of you.

God Bless, Dave Beckwith
**Beckwith for Congress** _Restoring Faith in the American Dream_

So now that they’ve failed to block the will of the people from being heard this November, they’re scrambling for new strategies to cheat their way into power.
One of their next big schemes is to target the census.

The Trump administration has already proposed changes to the census that would have cataclysmic impacts, from distorting the mapping process to making it harder for communities of color to access healthcare and vital services.

## Route 66 Turns 100

| | | Friend,No one could hear her. A young girl named Kristen was locked in an attic. No windows. No fresh air. No way out. The door was locked from the outside. For months she lived there.
Alone. There was no bathroom.
Just a bucket. No shower. No clean clothes. And the only time she left that attic was when she was sold for sex.
Over. And over. And over. **This is the reality of child trafficking.**

Millions of children are trapped in exploitation around the world. But Kristen's story did not end in that attic. One night she knocked on a hotel room door. Her trafficker had arranged and forced her into another "date." But instead...**she met a rescue team - Freedom Strike Force. **They were working alongside law enforcement to identify victims and traffickers. When Kristen realized she was safe... She collapsed into the arms of one of our female advocates. **Free.** Law enforcement then raided the house where she was held. Traffickers were arrested. Kristen was taken to a safe place. For the first time in months, she had a real bed and a hot meal**.**

**She took the first step toward healing.** **Because people like you chose to act, this rescue was possible.**

**Sound of Freedom Foundation** exists to _stop_ _ __the sale __of God 's children._ Inspired by the film _Sound of Freedom_ , the Foundation works around the world to **prevent trafficking, support rescue efforts, educate families, raise awareness, and push for stronger laws that protect children.** Our mission is simple. **To stop the sale of God 's children.** And right now we are preparing a new mission, happening in just a few weeks in Phoenix. Our **Freedom Strike Force** partner will train local law enforcement for two days, teaching them how to identify traffickers and victims hidden in plain sight. Then on day three...they go into the field. **Real operations. Real arrests. Real rescues.**

clean_body: A rescue team changed Kristen's life. Another mission begins in Phoenix. | | | | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | | Friend,No one could hear her. A young girl named Kristen was locked in an attic. No windows. No fresh air. No way out. The door was locked from the outside. For months she lived there. Alone. There was no bathroom. Just a bucket. No shower. No clean clothes. And the only time she left that attic was when she was sold for sex. Over. And over. And over. This is the reality of child trafficking. Millions of children are trapped in exploitation around the world. But Kristen's story did not end in that attic. One night she knocked on a hotel room door. Her trafficker had arranged and forced her into another "date." But instead...she met a rescue team - Freedom Strike Force. They were working alongside law enforcement to identify victims and traffickers. When Kristen realized she was safe... She collapsed into the arms of one of our female advocates. Free. Law enforcement then raided the house where she was held. Traffickers were arrested. Kristen was taken to a safe place. For the first time in months, she had a real bed and a hot meal. She took the first step toward healing. Because people like you chose to act, this rescue was possible. Sound of Freedom Foundation exists to stop the sale of God 's children. Inspired by the film Sound of Freedom , the Foundation works around the world to prevent trafficking, support rescue efforts, educate families, raise awareness, and push for stronger laws that protect children. Our mission is simple. To stop the sale of God 's children. And right now we are preparing a new mission, happening in just a few weeks in Phoenix. Our Freedom Strike Force partner will train local law enforcement for two days, teaching them how to identify traffickers and victims hidden in plain sight. Then on day three...they go into the field. Real operations. Real arrests. Real rescues. | | | | | | | | Children like Kristen are waiting. But these missions cannot happen without support from people who care. That is why I am reaching out to you today. Your donation today can help: Train officers to find trafficked children Support rescue operations Provide food, clothing, and care for survivors Help children begin the journey to healing When I first heard the stories of trafficked children, I asked myself a question. What if it were my child? I could not stay silent. And you do not have to either. Friend, will you please help rescue the next child today? Your gift -- whatever God places on your heart -- will help bring freedom to children still waiting in the dark. Together we can make sure more children hear the sound of Freedom. With gratitude and prayer, Eduardo Verastegui Sound of Freedom, Producer For Sound of Freedom Foundation P.S. The cost to staff, equip, and execute a Freedom Strike Force Training Camp is $25,000. disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JOSH GOTTHEIMER FOR CONGRESS
body:
---
| | Hi team,

Today, on Veterans Day, we pause to honor the brave men and women across New Jersey and our entire country who answered the call to serve.

**Our veterans put everything on the line to defend our freedom, protect our families, and keep our communities safe. Their dedication represents the best of who we are, and we must never take it for granted.**

Honoring our veterans isn’t just about the words we say on November 11th - it’s about following through on the promises we’ve made to them every single day. That means ensuring every veteran has access to quality healthcare, good-paying jobs, stable housing, and the full benefits they’ve earned without bureaucratic delays. We must always have the backs of those who have had ours.

To every veteran and military family in our community: thank you for your selfless service, your sacrifice, and your steadfast commitment to our nation.

— Josh
---

[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

In California’s 7th congressional district, Justice Democrat Mai Vang
narrowly lost her insurgent race against billionaire incumbent Rep. Doris
Matsui.

Mai — a principled, progressive leader on the Sacramento City Council —
was spurred to run by the dueling crises of affordability and ICE terror
that Matsui has failed to address for decades. She ran a fearless,
grassroots-backed campaign focused directly on serving her community.

To cling to power and become one of the five oldest members of the House,
Matsui transferred nearly $7 million of her personal wealth into her
campaign — a desperate, last-ditch step she has never taken in her prior
10 re-election campaigns. We fought back with pure grassroots power,
fueled by people who believed in Mai’s vision of healthcare, housing, and
dignity for all.

This race proved just how much of a threat our movement is to the
wealthiest and most entrenched political dynasties in the country. An
incumbent shouldn’t have to burn through millions of her own fortune just
for a chance to defeat a movement built by working people.

While Matsui empties her pockets to remain one of the most compromised and
ineffective members of Congress — bending to the whims of ICE and AIPAC
rather than serving her constituents — Mai will keep organizing on the
ground to protect Sacramento from the harms of their incumbent’s corporate
donors.

As our Executive Director Hodari Williams put it: “Mai represents the
future of this party, and Matsui represents the dying breaths of an
establishment in decline.”

What our movement accomplished this cycle is nothing short of incredible.
Despite the outcome of CA-07, this remains Justice Democrats’ most
successful cycle yet as we send 8 new progressive champions to Washington
to expand our bloc and build independent power for the working class
outside of Congress.

Thank you for standing with us in this fight every step of the
way, Peter. We couldn’t have done
it without you.

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats
