Peter,

Last week, we saw hundreds of women make history. Her Bold Move candidates have flipped Senate and House seats and shattered glass ceilings. They’ve won races in deep red districts in Alabama, West Virginia, Tennessee, Texas, Missouri, and many more. We are thrilled to report that so many of these victories will chip away at GOP male supermajorities in state legislatures that have passed restrictive abortion laws.

**At HBM, we had historic wins for women candidates around the country:**
---
* In 2026 alone, Her Bold Move endorsed 137 candidates across 33 states.
* 85% of those candidates WON (so far) and will be seated in elected offices in 28 states!
* 65% of Her Bold Move’s candidates won seats in state legislatures with male SUPERmajorities. That means there will be fewer men in these state governments and more opportunities for women to collaborate with each other.
* 59% of Her Bold Move’s winning candidates won in states with abortion bans

---
Now, as we look forward to 2027, there will be more women and women of color in the halls of power in America than ever before. Last week, CA-45 sent me back to Washington, and a lot of new Democratic colleagues are coming with me. Democrats will hold majorities in both the House and the Senate. **[So as we get to work, I have one request, and it isn’t a donation. I want to know what you think we should do first. Will you take two minutes to fill out my 2027 priorities survey?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143296561/659735977/344790957?refcode=em-11.11.26-all-b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiODgyZjNkZWEtZjlkZC1mMTExLTkxZjUtMDAyMjQ4MjRkOWY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=FkXA3aj7AEynU4twaw5B4Ecj5fK4LAU0izujdid0frU=&emci=862f3dea-f9dd-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&emdi=882f3dea-f9dd-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&ceid=27336212)** | **[Take the Survey](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143296563/659735979/344790957?refcode=em-11.11.26-all-b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiODgyZjNkZWEtZjlkZC1mMTExLTkxZjUtMDAyMjQ4MjRkOWY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=FkXA3aj7AEynU4twaw5B4Ecj5fK4LAU0izujdid0frU=&emci=862f3dea-f9dd-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&emdi=882f3dea-f9dd-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&ceid=27336212)**

There’s a lot of work waiting for us. Families here in Orange and LA County are feeling the Medicaid and SNAP cuts, and more than 20 million Americans are paying more for healthcare coverage without the ACA tax credits that kept their premiums affordable. Michelle and I own a pharmacy here in the district, so when Medicaid or ACA coverage changes, we see it at the counter.
Trump’s tariffs are still driving up the cost of everyday goods, and the federal minimum wage has been stuck at $7.25 since 2009. Beyond costs, a Democratic Congress can protect reproductive freedom, pass the PRO Act for workers who want to organize, and finally use its war powers to end the war with Iran.
But I don’t want to guess which of these matters most. I’d rather hear it from you. My team and I will go through every response, and what you tell us will shape where I put my energy when the new Congress starts.

Fourteen months ago, we set out to prove something: that a daughter of Hmong refugees from South Sacramento, with no corporate PAC money, could take on one of the most entrenched political operations in California.

We were outspent 8 to 1, and we never backed down.

Young people, voters of color, and Democrats who had spent years on the sidelines showed up at record levels. More than a thousand volunteers knocked doors and made calls. Thousands of neighbors gave whatever they could. Thousands voted for the first time — some waiting in long lines to cast their ballot.

Ua tsaug. Thank you.

Our region's politics have changed for good because of you.

And make no mistake about the role big money played in this race. The ten-term incumbent spent $7 million of her own money to buy back her seat in Congress. AIPAC and corporate PACs spent hundreds of thousands more to drive up Republican turnout and spread disinformation about our campaign.

**And yet — for the first time since 1978, someone other than a Matsui won Sacramento County. A majority of Democrats chose our movement over the officially endorsed party candidate. That is not a loss. That is an earthquake.**

But I won't pretend the stakes aren't high, because they have never been higher. Stephen Miller, the architect of mass deportations, now runs the White House, and ICE is still terrorizing families in our neighborhoods. Our immigrant communities cannot afford a representative who waits to act. Millions are losing their health coverage. Our tax dollars still fund war and genocide. And families across this region are living paycheck to paycheck.

The demand for Medicare for All has never been louder — and this election made one thing clear: our region is ready for change.

Doris Matsui told this district she delivers. We will hold her accountable every single step of the way.

And I will keep fighting — for the people of this region, for Medicare for All, for an end to deportations and family separations, and for a future where every family knows they belong.

We are not going anywhere. For the movement we've built together, this is only the beginning.

The world we envision is on her way.

With heart and hustle,

Mai

| |
---
Mai is the daughter of Hmong refugees, born and raised in Sacramento. Mai’s parents fled war in Laos and arrived in California to find a new life.

As the oldest of 16 children, she helped raise her siblings while working hard to build a career dedicated to helping her community thrive. Mai is a proud product of public schools and was the first in her family to attend college. As a young organizer, Mai returned home to serve the community that raised and supported her.

name: MassDems featuring Senator John Velis & Representative Shirley Arriaga
subject: Happy Veterans Day
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Massachusetts Democratic State Committee Massachusetts Democratic Party
body:
| | | |
---
| | | Dear Friends, Today, as we recognize Veterans Day, we join together to honor the extraordinary courage, dedication, and sacrifices of the men and women who have served our nation. Veterans have answered the call to serve, putting their lives on the line to defend our freedoms, protect our democracy, and uphold the values that define our country. Their commitment to our nation does not end when they return home, and neither should our commitment to supporting them and their families. Massachusetts has a proud history of standing up for our veterans, and we remain committed to ensuring that those who served receive the recognition, resources, and opportunities they have earned. In the Legislature, working in collaboration with the Healey-Driscoll Administration, and our Congressional delegation, our Commonwealth has taken important steps to strengthen support for Veterans, including:
---
| | |
* **Expanding access to services:** Massachusetts is home to approximately 274,000 veterans, including an estimated 42,000 in Western Massachusetts. The first ever regional office of the Executive Office of Veterans Services opened in Springfield this month and will provide in-person assistance with benefits, housing resources, mental health support, and connections to local organizations. Likewise, the ribbon cutting of the new Holyoke Veterans Home this fall, and the continued enhancements at the Chelsea Veterans Home, represent a historic new chapter of long-term care from the Commonwealth for veterans and their families.
* **Creating new employment opportunities:** The administration recently established the Veterans Employment Opportunities Commission (VEOC) to identify barriers to employment and expand career opportunities for veterans and military families.
* **Delivering meaningful financial assistance:** More than 23,300 eligible disabled veterans, Gold Star parents and spouses, and surviving spouses received an annual $2,500 tax-free benefit this year, totaling $58.4 million in payments. This represented a 10% increase in recipients and the largest year-over-year increase in the program's history.
* **Passage of the HERO Act:** (Honoring, Empowering, and Recognizing our Service members & Veterans) is the most comprehensive veterans' legislation in Massachusetts history, delivering more than 30 initiatives to expand benefits, improve access to mental health care, strengthen employment opportunities, and provide greater financial support for veterans and their families. By modernizing veterans' services, expanding protections and benefits, supporting military-connected students and families, and ensuring greater inclusion for veterans of all backgrounds, Massachusetts is once again setting a national standard for honoring those who have served our country.

---
| | | While these investments represent important progress, our work is far from finished. We must continue expanding access to affordable housing, quality health care, mental health services, meaningful employment, and the benefits that veterans and military families deserve. Supporting our veterans means recognizing that the responsibilities we owe them extend well beyond their years in uniform. It requires sustained leadership, meaningful investments, and a willingness to listen to veterans and their families about the challenges they face every day. On this Veterans Day, we extend our deepest gratitude to every veteran who has worn our nation's uniform and to the families who have shared in their sacrifices. Thank you for your service, your courage, and your unwavering commitment to our country. We will never take your sacrifices for granted, and we remain unwavering in our commitment to ensuring that Massachusetts continues to lead the nation in standing up for our veterans, active-duty service members, and military families. They have always answered the call for us, and we must always answer the call for them. Sincerely,
---
State Senator John Velis, U.S. Army Veteran; Massachusetts National GuardState Representative Shirley Arriaga, U.S. Air Force Veteran

Friend, Our veterans and their families serve our country and deserve a government that serves them in return. But, right now, the 1.3 million veterans who rely on SNAP (the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) to afford groceries are seeing a devastating cut due to last year’s Big Betrayal Bill.1,2 **Additionally, combat-injured veterans who receive disability compensation are currently seeing a reduction in their retirement pay.** Both policies need to change. **Right now, I’m working with colleagues to force a vote on a bipartisan bill that would eliminate the “veterans’ tax” by ensuring combat-injured veterans receive their full retirement along with their full disability compensation, rewriting rules that penalize veterans for receiving both payments at the same time.**
Additionally, when Democrats retake control of Congress next year, we need to urgently work to undo SNAP cuts that impact veterans and non-veterans alike. **The Big Betrayal Bill, which was Trump's one big legislative victory last year, eliminated a protection that helped veterans keep their SNAP benefits, regardless of SNAP’s work-reporting requirements.** It also imposed enormous new costs on states, threatening food assistance for millions of people.
These cuts and cost shifts have already resulted in 5.5 million people losing their SNAP benefits, including at least 1.5 million children.3 When states cannot afford the costs congressional Republicans have handed them, people struggling to afford groceries pay the price or states take the money from other critical programs.
Veterans and disabled-veterans who served our country deserve full benefits, not cuts and offsets. According to the Pentagon’s own reporting, one in four military families faces food insecurity, struggling to consistently put food on the table.1
**These policies are cruelty by design.** No one should be forced to go without, particularly to pay for more tax breaks for billionaires and corporations.

# [Nvidia's China spy nightmare explodes with National Security implications](https://substack.com/redirect/0ac2b2bc-2117-48ff-8bdb-82418618adfb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nvidia's board opened an investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort after reports tied him to Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive **[U.S. officials believed had been recruited](https://substack.com/redirect/177ed221-6fd1-4c22-abc3-0e01ced29f32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** by China's Ministry of State Security. **[A May short-seller report](https://substack.com/redirect/8e0bde2d-59da-411a-9808-3eee8287dec4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** had already **[called the relationship uncomfortably close.](https://substack.com/redirect/35d0acb8-0b0b-40bc-8ec8-9846b61c3be8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9844b4ed-d831-4a8d-91d5-2994057ba1a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Nvidia 's board** launched an independent investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort after reports linked him to Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive U.S. officials believed had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security.
* **Culper Research** (founded by Christian Lamarco in 2019 and named after George Washington's Revolutionary War spy ring) published its May 2026 report "NVIDIA (NVDA): The China Problem," flagging an "uncomfortably close" relationship and alleging Megaspeed was financed by Alibaba through shell companies.
* **A current Megaspeed** employee said Huang visits the company's linked data centers every few months and is always accompanied by Alibaba representatives, describing the relationship as "very close"; a former Nvidia employee said many staff had wondered if there was a special relationship.
* **A secret State Department memo** based on electronic surveillance alleged Alice Huang was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security and worked to gain Huang's favor partly through purchases of billions of dollars of Nvidia chips for AI data centers in the Middle East and Southeast Asia.
* **Culper cited** photos of the two together in June 2024 and May 2025, claimed Megaspeed was the largest buyer of Nvidia chips in Southeast Asia and faced U.S. and Singapore investigations over possible diversion, and said Chinese firms were accessing advanced AI chips through Southeast Asian buyers amid export controls.
* **Nvidia 's board** said independent counsel and directors would handle the inquiry, retained confidence in Huang's leadership, and stated it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised while prioritizing U.S. national and economic security.

# [Analyst cuts Nvidia to "Neutral" on spy scandal uncertainties](https://substack.com/redirect/0ac2b2bc-2117-48ff-8bdb-82418618adfb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Baird analyst Tristan Gerra **[downgraded Nvidia to Neutral](https://substack.com/redirect/b893ecb8-a1e0-4322-a33b-12c3dce1ff5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in a note titled "Icarus' Rise and Fall; Company Will be Fine," citing unresolved uncertainties around government action, investigations, revenue impact, and CEO tenure after Huang admitted an affair.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0ac2b2bc-2117-48ff-8bdb-82418618adfb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Gerra 's conditions:** He is cutting the rating until uncertainties from an upcoming congressional hearing are lifted, U.S. government investigations conclude, revenue impact from near-term channel adjustments and potential charges is quantified, and questions around CEO tenure clear.
* **Write-down risk:** Gerra highlighted a new ban on H200 exports to China and said low-level shipping into Asia-based warehouses with inventories awaiting China demand could translate into a $5 billion write-down.
* **Export controls:** He noted export control limitations addressing Southeast Asia data center loopholes, plus potential DOJ action against Megaspeed and resulting preemptive or enforced steps by other regional operators with China demand exposure.
* **Stock move:** Shares are down about 12% since the situation became public. Nvidia closed at 168.89 on Nov. 10, down 5.47%.

# [CFTC probes Kalshi for improper self-certification of event contracts](https://substack.com/redirect/0ac2b2bc-2117-48ff-8bdb-82418618adfb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is investigating whether prediction-market platform Kalshi **[improperly self-certified event contracts](https://substack.com/redirect/8708e9bd-6585-41aa-8920-d78f1f779cb1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/8708e9bd-6585-41aa-8920-d78f1f779cb1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)by failing to properly inform the agency of proposed contracts. Kalshi called it a minor filing issue and said it is working with the agency.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0ac2b2bc-2117-48ff-8bdb-82418618adfb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Kalshi response:** Head of communications Elisabeth Diana said the notice is about a procedural error involving the submission of a handful of contracts, many of which weren't live, and that the company is already addressing the issue. The CFTC flagged weather-related contracts.
* **Self-certification rules:** Platforms may self-certify event contracts without prior federal approval if they comply with the Commodity Exchange Act, allowing faster introduction of new contracts. Politico first reported the probe, noting charges could come soon based on a private CFTC notification.
* **Prior actions:** In August the CFTC ordered Kalshi to take down sports-related mention markets while it examined the contract type. The agency is also probing competitor Polymarket over whether it violated a 2022 settlement barring U.S. traders from its international platform.
* **Congressional heat:** Rep. Ro Khanna called on X for a ban on sports prediction markets, which account for the overwhelming majority of volume on leading platforms. Heightened scrutiny is expected once the Democratic Congress is sworn in in January.

# [CoreWeave CEO: Dem midterm sweep won't slow our AI data-center build](https://substack.com/redirect/0ac2b2bc-2117-48ff-8bdb-82418618adfb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

He expects no impact and plans to keep scaling as good neighbors.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0ac2b2bc-2117-48ff-8bdb-82418618adfb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* **Intrator quotes:** He said the company does not anticipate any impact from the seismic regulatory shift, believes what occurred is a statement around how you build, and wants to build responsibly. He added CoreWeave is very comfortable with its pipeline and sees an opportunity to continue scaling within the new political reality.
* **Election results:** Democrats won control of both houses of Congress and governors' races in key AI states including Texas, Ohio and Georgia. Voters sided in favor of greater restrictions on data centers in 40 of 41 ballot measures across 10 states on Nov. 3.
* **Buildout targets:** CoreWeave reported 168% year-over-year revenue growth, beating estimates, and lifted its 2026 forecast. It anticipates 1.85 gigawatts in active power by the end of 2026 and is targeting $37 billion to $39 billion in full-year capital expenditures for 2026.
* **Market reaction:** The company said the regulatory environment is a statement on responsible building rather than a barrier to growth.

# [Goolsbee: October CPI is "borderline disturbing"](https://substack.com/redirect/0ac2b2bc-2117-48ff-8bdb-82418618adfb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee called the latest consumer price report **["borderline disturbing" and "distressing,"](https://substack.com/redirect/0152516e-4722-4d67-a591-a00e27a77443?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/0152516e-4722-4d67-a591-a00e27a77443?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)saying the central bank has a real inflation issue on its hands that has been developing and will have to be dealt with.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0ac2b2bc-2117-48ff-8bdb-82418618adfb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **CPI print:** The consumer price index rose 0.4% on a seasonally adjusted basis in October, higher than economists predicted and the third straight month of outsized price increases. Goolsbee said he had not seen tariff-related price drivers fade as hoped and remained concerned about continuously high services inflation.
* **Other officials:** Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a hot inflation report could push him toward advocating a half-point increase in December if core CPI was around 0.3. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said she sees a need for two additional quarter-point increases and that it may be possible to move more rapidly this winter.
* **Goolsbee caution:** He said lofty prices are on everyone's mind--businesses, nonprofits and ordinary consumers--and that the possibility of inflation expectations rising is a major concern that could make cooling prices much more painful. He declined to specify a December move, saying he is not a fan of tying the committee's hands.
* **Market pricing:** Fed funds futures now unanimously expect a rate hike at the December meeting. Odds of a half-point hike stand at 15%, with a 60% chance rates reach 4.25%-4.5% by the January meeting.

Analyst cuts Nvidia to "Neutral" on spy scandal uncertainties | | | Nov 11| | | ∙| | Guest post ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | Nvidia's board opened an investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort after reports tied him to Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive by China's Ministry of State Security. had already | | ---|---|--- Nvidia 's board launched an independent investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort after reports linked him to Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive U.S. officials believed had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security. Culper Research (founded by Christian Lamarco in 2019 and named after George Washington's Revolutionary War spy ring) published its May 2026 report "NVIDIA (NVDA): The China Problem," flagging an "uncomfortably close" relationship and alleging Megaspeed was financed by Alibaba through shell companies. A current Megaspeed employee said Huang visits the company's linked data centers every few months and is always accompanied by Alibaba representatives, describing the relationship as "very close"; a former Nvidia employee said many staff had wondered if there was a special relationship. A secret State Department memo based on electronic surveillance alleged Alice Huang was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security and worked to gain Huang's favor partly through purchases of billions of dollars of Nvidia chips for AI data centers in the Middle East and Southeast Asia. Culper cited photos of the two together in June 2024 and May 2025, claimed Megaspeed was the largest buyer of Nvidia chips in Southeast Asia and faced U.S. and Singapore investigations over possible diversion, and said Chinese firms were accessing advanced AI chips through Southeast Asian buyers amid export controls. Nvidia 's board said independent counsel and directors would handle the inquiry, retained confidence in Huang's leadership, and stated it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised while prioritizing U.S. national and economic security. | | ---|---|--- The climb ahead is steep and the market can be cruel. But Americans built fortunes from raw ambition! The railroad barons who opened a continent, the oil wildcatters who drilled through dry holes until the gusher hit, the traders who turned American free enterprise into the world's capital of capital. They went through worse and they bet everything on the American idea that markets and drive create wealth. We will not watch that edge get dulled. We press for prosperity every session, even through the drawdowns, the way the builders of this country did. All of us here at The Capitalist loyalty and time you take to read us everyday, so we make this promise to you. Your money matters. We will staff the desks that bring you the news and information that matters so you can do what you do best, build your American Dream. | | | | ---|---|--- | 5:58 PM | Baird analyst Tristan Gerra in a note titled "Icarus' Rise and Fall; Company Will be Fine," citing unresolved uncertainties around government action, investigations, revenue impact, and CEO tenure after Huang admitted an affair. | | ---|---|--- Gerra 's conditions: He is cutting the rating until uncertainties from an upcoming congressional hearing are lifted, U.S. government investigations conclude, revenue impact from near-term channel adjustments and potential charges is quantified, and questions around CEO tenure clear. Write-down risk: Gerra highlighted a new ban on H200 exports to China and said low-level shipping into Asia-based warehouses with inventories awaiting China demand could translate into a $5 billion write-down. Export controls: He noted export control limitations addressing Southeast Asia data center loopholes, plus potential DOJ action against Megaspeed and resulting preemptive or enforced steps by other regional operators with China demand exposure. Stock move: Shares are down about 12% since the situation became public. Nvidia closed at 168.89 on Nov. 10, down 5.47%. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was reportedly after U.S. officials concluded Iranian plotting against current and former American officials had reached a more advanced stage. He leads Operation Economic Outcast, launched in August to isolate Iran economically. Indictments filed: The Justice Department said late Tuesday that three Iranian nationals have been indicted on terrorism-related charges involving nearly 20 attacks and attempted attacks across Europe and the United States, including a September attack targeting RAF Fairford in the U.K. where U.S. personnel were stationed. Officials ' comments: Attorney General Todd Blanche said anyone who plans a terrorist plot on a military base housing American servicemembers will be prosecuted by the United States government. Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly said military action against Iran may not be necessary if sanctions and the naval blockade are proving effective. Trump remarks: On Monday Trump posted that Qatar, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait and others would prefer the status quo, a continuation of the Greatest Naval Blockade in History, and that positive momentum was visible toward an end to the conflict. On Tuesday he said he wanted to ensure U.S. allies were not hurt and that there was a long-term solution. Oil prices: Brent crude was about $92 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate about $86 in Wednesday's Asia trading session. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is investigating whether prediction-market platform Kalshi failing to properly inform the agency of proposed contracts. Kalshi called it a minor filing issue and said it is working with the agency. | | ---|---|--- Kalshi response: Head of communications Elisabeth Diana said the notice is about a procedural error involving the submission of a handful of contracts, many of which weren't live, and that the company is already addressing the issue. The CFTC flagged weather-related contracts. Self-certification rules: Platforms may self-certify event contracts without prior federal approval if they comply with the Commodity Exchange Act, allowing faster introduction of new contracts. Politico first reported the probe, noting charges could come soon based on a private CFTC notification. Prior actions: In August the CFTC ordered Kalshi to take down sports-related mention markets while it examined the contract type. The agency is also probing competitor Polymarket over whether it violated a 2022 settlement barring U.S. traders from its international platform. Congressional heat: Rep. Ro Khanna called on X for a ban on sports prediction markets, which account for the overwhelming majority of volume on leading platforms. Heightened scrutiny is expected once the Democratic Congress is sworn in in January. CoreWeave CEO Mike Intrator said after Democrats swept midterms and voters backed data-center restrictions will not slow the company's AI infrastructure expansion. He expects no impact and plans to keep scaling as good neighbors. | | ---|---|--- Intrator quotes: He said the company does not anticipate any impact from the seismic regulatory shift, believes what occurred is a statement around how you build, and wants to build responsibly. He added CoreWeave is very comfortable with its pipeline and sees an opportunity to continue scaling within the new political reality. Election results: Democrats won control of both houses of Congress and governors' races in key AI states including Texas, Ohio and Georgia. Voters sided in favor of greater restrictions on data centers in 40 of 41 ballot measures across 10 states on Nov. 3. Buildout targets: CoreWeave reported 168% year-over-year revenue growth, beating estimates, and lifted its 2026 forecast. It anticipates 1.85 gigawatts in active power by the end of 2026 and is targeting $37 billion to $39 billion in full-year capital expenditures for 2026. Market reaction: The company said the regulatory environment is a statement on responsible building rather than a barrier to growth. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee called the latest consumer price report the central bank has a real inflation issue on its hands that has been developing and will have to be dealt with. | | ---|---|--- CPI print: The consumer price index rose 0.4% on a seasonally adjusted basis in October, higher than economists predicted and the third straight month of outsized price increases. Goolsbee said he had not seen tariff-related price drivers fade as hoped and remained concerned about continuously high services inflation. Other officials: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a hot inflation report could push him toward advocating a half-point increase in December if core CPI was around 0.3. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said she sees a need for two additional quarter-point increases and that it may be possible to move more rapidly this winter. Goolsbee caution: He said lofty prices are on everyone's mind--businesses, nonprofits and ordinary consumers--and that the possibility of inflation expectations rising is a major concern that could make cooling prices much more painful. He declined to specify a December move, saying he is not a fan of tying the committee's hands. Market pricing: Fed funds futures now unanimously expect a rate hike at the December meeting. Odds of a half-point hike stand at 15%, with a 60% chance rates reach 4.25%-4.5% by the January meeting. Anthropic ahead of its IPO, including Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets in beta and Claude Dashboards (now Claude Data) to general availability. The tools extend functionality within Claude and are available on all paid plans. | | ---|---|--- Overlap noted: Claude Whiteboards turns team discussions into boards with deliverables, timelines and assignments, overlapping with Monday.com, Asana and Zoom Whiteboard. Claude Meetings, coming soon, overlaps with those companies' AI notetaker and meeting-summary tools by transcribing calls, updating documents and taking actions. Limitations cited: Whiteboards act as a snapshot without ongoing tracking, automation or admin controls, allowing Monday.com and Asana to retain advantages in work execution. Zoom's tools handle transcription and workflows across platforms without a bot in some cases. Stock reaction: Monday.com, Asana and Zoom all traded lower on Tuesday. Microsoft shares fell 2.2% on fears of rivalry with its Office franchise, though analysts do not expect meaningful near-term impact on Microsoft 365 growth given deep enterprise integration and commitments to security and IP sovereignty. body:
Judicial Watch announced that it forced the release of 142 pages
of new, heavily-redacted Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) records
through a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit concerning Thomas
Matthew Crooks, the gunman who attempted to assassinate
then-presidential candidate Donald Trump at a July 2024 campaign rally
in Butler, Pennsylvania.

in Butler, Pennsylvania. The records reveal that Venmo suspended
Crooks’ account for “unusual activity” the day after the
assassination attempt, the FBI submitted a request for foreign
dissemination of information about images found on Crooks’
electronic devices, and PayPal repeatedly addressed him as “Rod
Swanson” in emails.

Dear Patriot,
Nearly twenty years in this work has taught me one rule about Washington: **When a door opens, someone is already pushing it shut.** Senator Rand Paul opened one for us. Send subpoena requests to his office . . . the one office in the Senate with sole power to issue them. **No reporter has ever held a key like this.** Since then, you and I have a responsibility to build something fast: A small team of researchers and professionals must be funded and put to work right now. Threads picked: the ballot cash. The border money. The Pfizer papers. And one twenty-year theory, at last ready for its test. Now for the truth about doors . . . Gavels change hands. Sessions end. And the first time a return comes back with a big name on it, they will push hard to shut this down. Harder than we have ever felt. **Senator Paul 's offer has no closing date printed on it. Washington will print one for us if we move slow.** So we will not move slow. name: Autism Health
subject: Honoring Our Veterans On Veterans Day
body:
** Honoring Our Veterans On Veterans Day
------------------------------------------------------------

Today, November 11, we pause to honor the brave men and women who have worn the uniform of the United States Armed Forces and dedicated themselves to protecting our nation, our freedoms, and the values we hold dear.

As a proud United States Air Force veteran, Veterans Day holds a special place in my heart. Having served our country, I understand firsthand the commitment, sacrifice, and sense of duty that come with military service. It is an honor to stand alongside those who have answered the call to serve.

At Autism Health, we recognize that service and sacrifice extend beyond the individual veteran. Military spouses, children, and families also make tremendous sacrifices, often facing unique challenges while supporting their loved ones. We especially acknowledge our military families raising children with autism and other developmental disabilities, whose strength, resilience, and dedication deserve recognition.

Today, we extend our deepest gratitude to every veteran, past and present, for your courage, commitment, and willingness to serve something greater than yourself.

To my fellow veterans: Thank you for your service. Your sacrifices will never be forgotten.

May God bless our veterans, our military families, and the United States of America.

With Heartfelt Gratitude,
Tracy Slepcevic
U.S. Air Force Veteran
Co-Founder & President, Autism Health Inc.
Author, Warrior Mom: A Mother's Journey in Healing Her Son with Autism

www.AutismHealth.com (https://click.mailchimp.com/track/click/30010842/www.autismhealth.com?&mc_cid=360dbf7ac2&mc_eid=UNIQID)

| | | | Fellow Patriot, **[I was just charged with TWO FELONIES for my undercover journalism in Minnesota.](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckc2OmzAQgJ_G3EB47PBz8CENoUrVrKo9pEdr8A9rCdsIO-zrV2ybF-icRp_m79P8vss7usWF-Q29EWp3ckvSubCblN2M2WjvQjApZgzxU0INTUlpSalEld1uJMdCC6UbBoURtO05B2g5FB-iZZr2YMFYznsKqNoOYULN-obZ1rLCiWMcPaLjJ9ZXTV-rqbNoprpXtT0RXj9XjdmkSsWQzLbjsdOFEI8shkpFXyziI-c1EXYmMBIYdQyYTRX9bKu4zQTGFTmdOpxYx1oArRutmKWEjc_sZYrPTRnChvfrg0BzIG-0e3rChuv9fPv5Dyr0K7o5EDb8Pbs-yW_Dd3n5Mcr360N-1cr723Ady1_n8vK4vRpjyCZkwobL41a-lItN6PXTLYtLTUt4PXt0y5dP_s837AL-BAAA__9KlZSs)** **Back in August, we published a********bombshell investigative report on voter vouching laws****.****We never cast a ballot. As of the newest count: **4,250** , growing with every batch as ballots from Alaska's rural and Native communities arrive and are counted. The GOP’s entire legal strategy — the DOJ lawsuit, the certification challenge, the appeal — was built on one premise: that Mary might win by fewer votes than the ballot dispute involves. **Her lead is now larger than that.** Here's what remains: at least 37,000 votes still to count, a major batch expected Friday, and the official ranked-choice tabulation on November 18, where the preliminary data already shows Mary winning, before thousands of rural ballots that broke two-to-one her way are even factored in. Every trend points one direction: toward the fifth win, the completed sweep, and a Yup'ik leader joining the first Native woman ever seated in the U.S. Senate. subject: A message on Veterans Day

body:
Paid for by Nick Brown for Attorney General [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP59/1/106966/images/NWB%20Logo%20%28Resized%29.png]
Peter,

Today, on Veterans Day, I’m thinking about the men and women who have worn our nation’s uniform, the families who have stood behind them, and the sacrifices they have made in service to our country.

I know that service comes with a responsibility unlike any other. I joined ROTC to help pay for college, and after law school, I became an officer in the U.S. Army JAG Corps. I served in Iraq, where I worked to defend the rights of American soldiers serving thousands of miles from home.

I saw firsthand what it means to put on a uniform and accept the possibility that you may not make it home. I saw the commitment, courage, and sense of duty that service members bring to their work, often under circumstances most Americans will never experience.

And today, those sacrifices are once again playing out in the Middle East.

The United States is at war with Iran, a conflict this administration chose to enter and one that continues to put American service members in danger. As someone who has served in a war zone, I know that decisions made in Washington, D.C. have consequences that extend far beyond the halls of the White House and the Pentagon.

There are American sons and daughters thousands of miles from home, facing real dangers and carrying out orders that could cost them their lives. There are parents, spouses, and children waiting for them to return safely. And there are military families once again living with the uncertainty that comes with having someone they love in uniform.

We cannot lose sight of the people behind the headlines and military briefings. We cannot treat the lives of American service members as an afterthought in decisions about war. Our leaders have a responsibility to be thoughtful about the decisions they make and the risks they ask our military to take.

This Veterans Day, I’m especially grateful to everyone who has answered the call to serve, to the families who have shared in that sacrifice, and to those who never made it home.

To all who have served, and to all who are serving today, thank you. Our country owes you more than words can express.

– Nick Brown

| | | Hi Peter,
---
Happy Veterans Day to all who’ve served our country. Thank you for your sacrifice and your belief that the promise of America is worth defending.
Today, I'm honoring Virginia's veterans at the Virginia War Memorial. It's a quiet, powerful place, and every time I'm there I'm struck by how many Virginians have given so much.
Our Veterans make great sacrifices to keep our Commonwealth and our country safe — and as Governor, I’m proud to stand up for Virginia’s servicemembers and their families.
Our responsibility to our veterans doesn't end when the uniform comes off, and I intend to see that Virginia keeps showing up for them with the strongest possible support.
To every veteran reading this, and to the families who stood behind them: thank you. I'm so grateful for you.
With gratitude,
Abigail

clean_body: [ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo Peter Willis, Today — Veterans Day — is a day to honor the people who have served our country and remember the enormous human cost of war. Instead, Congress is putting our servicemembers at risk as it RACES to pass Trump's $1.5 TRILLION request to fund the Pentagon during the lame duck. This massive defense bill would keep the billions coming for Trump's disastrous war against Iran, while authorizing HUNDREDS OF MILLIONS of dollars in bombs and weapons to Israel. [ ]Headline: After Midterms, Congress Returns to Reckon with Defense Funding, NDAA In our latest survey, Our Revolution members made their priorities unmistakably clear: the number one issue they want Democrats to act on NOW is stopping Trump's Iran war and stopping sending bombs to Israel. The first step is stopping Congress from rubber-stamping this record-shattering budget for the Pentagon — and it's going to take massive public outcry to do it. [ ]SIGN NOW: Tell Congress to stop funding Trump's war in Iran and block further weapons transfers to Israel, NOW! [ ]STOP FUNDING THE WAR [ ]Photo of protestors at a rally holding a banner reading: No War with Iran. Stop the 1% The Pentagon's own casualty figures show that 23 U.S. service members have died and 865 have been wounded in operations related to the Iran war. Meanwhile, the cost of this conflict keeps climbing, while families here at home face rising prices and the consequences of another open-ended military intervention. Now that Congress is back in Washington, one of its biggest unfinished jobs is the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), the annual defense policy bill. It already passed the House, and now Congress is sprinting to pass the bill in the next few weeks. Instead of handing Trump BILLIONS more for his warmongering, Congress must use this bill to halt support for the Iran war and end the flow of offensive weapons to Israel. Our Revolution is organizing to make sure the incoming Democratic majority hears the message loud and clear: voters want an end to endless war, not another blank check for the Pentagon and weapons contractors. This Veterans Day, honoring those who served means demanding that our leaders take the human costs of war seriously. It means diplomacy over escalation, accountability over blank checks, and investments in people's lives instead of more weapons and destruction. Peter,

Tomorrow is Randy’s birthday -- here’s a little inside joke from our team.

On Randy’s birthday last year, we said his real present wouldn’t arrive until a year later, November 2026, when the Central Valley would send him to Congress. It felt like a long shot at the time, but thanks to supporters like you, his gift showed up right on schedule!

So this year we get to celebrate his birthday and a historic win that so many people said couldn’t happen. And we want Randy to hear directly from the people who made it possible.

**Here's the bottom line:** We can’t defeat Donald Trump and return to the status quo. We must confront the extreme concentration of wealth and power in America. That starts by getting big money out of politics and building an economy that works for working people. We need to pass a 5% wealth tax on billionaires to fund universal childcare, education, and economic opportunity. We need to end endless foreign wars. And stand up to powerful interests, even when they fight back. **FDR confronted the economic royalists of his time—we need that same courage today.** I believe our generation can deliver America's Next New Deal. But we need a movement of people willing to demand it. Please [listen](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143299561/659746639/-1652675427?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDMyMDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjhlYTE3YmItMDlkZS1mMTExLTkxZjUtMDAyMjQ4MjRkOWY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=7kNhEIw-MzCht-EH1nN3v8HbTL_7JhCKp8t9hiIGVQ0=&emci=b6ea17bb-09de-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&emdi=b8ea17bb-09de-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&ceid=9848080) to our conversation and share it with someone who believes we can build a better future. name: Ryan Grim
subject: They said it was traffic
body:
This week showed exactly why Congress needs coverage written for the public, not lobbyists.

| |
---|---|---
|
# They said it was traffic
### This week showed exactly why Congress needs coverage written for the public, not lobbyists.
| | | [Drop Site News](https://substack.com/@dropsitenews)
---
| Nov 11
---
| [](https://substack.com/@dropsitenews)
---
Last week, I told you Drop Site is going to Capitol Hill.
The newsletters that cover Congress today are written for lobbyists and insiders, and funded by the industries most affected by what Congress does. So we're launching new Capitol Hill coverage written for the public, telling you what Congress is planning before the votes happen, not after.
We set out to raise $100,000 to launch it ahead of the December 11 war funding deadline. Readers responded fast. We've already raised over $80,000, more than 80% of the way there.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/77aa2d41-6895-40c1-a771-704b6b5dd611?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now we're turning to you to help close the gap.
**[For the next 48 hours, every new paid subscription goes directly toward launching our Capitol Hill coverage, and annual subscriptions are 20% off.](https://substack.com/redirect/77aa2d41-6895-40c1-a771-704b6b5dd611?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
That's less than $0.25 a day to put the public back in the room.
[UPGRADE NOW - 20% OFF!](https://substack.com/redirect/77aa2d41-6895-40c1-a771-704b6b5dd611?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
#### **What 's happening while no one is watching**
On Election Day, voters sent a clear message: end the war. Even JD Vance said so. Yet top Democrats and Republicans are quietly working to pass a spending bill before December 11 that would make a real fight over war funding impossible. You'd struggle to learn that from Punchbowl, Politico, or Axios.
This week showed what we're up against. On Tuesday, the House voted 211-204 to send Rep. Thomas Massie's articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to committee, where they can sit indefinitely. Eleven Democrats missed the vote. Had they shown up, the House would have been forced to vote on impeachment itself.
Several blamed traffic. Our colleague Julian Andreone was there and saw nothing impeding it. Meanwhile, the vote opened at 5:30 pm, in the middle of a 4:30 to 6:30 pm "new member reception" hosted by Elect Democratic Women, whose offshoot, EDW Action Fund, served as one of the major pass-throughs for AIPAC money in the primaries.
As Democrats fight over whether Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries should lead them, the insider newsletters will cover it as palace intrigue. We'll cover who's funding whom, and who skipped which vote and why.
**Washington is noticing.** This week, Semafor wrote that what's "worth watching most closely right now" in that fight is how independent outlets, Drop Site among them, approach it.
I co-wrote HuffPost Hill for years, back when it was the one Capitol Hill newsletter written for a mass audience. Everyone read it because everyone read it, and it broke news the others missed. **[We're building that again.](https://substack.com/redirect/77aa2d41-6895-40c1-a771-704b6b5dd611?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **
[FUND OUR HILL COVERAGE - 20% OFF](https://substack.com/redirect/77aa2d41-6895-40c1-a771-704b6b5dd611?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
#### **Why we 're asking you**
More than 830,000 people subscribe to Drop Site. We keep our reporting free to read, because the public should never have to pay to know what its government is doing.
But free journalism isn't free to produce. Fewer than three in every 100 readers pay for a subscription, and that small group carries the newsroom. They're why we answer to no corporate owner and take no editorial direction from donors, advertisers, or anyone else.
If you've been reading for free and meaning to upgrade, this is the moment it counts the most. [Your subscription in the next 48 hours goes straight to getting a reporting team on Capitol Hill before the December votes.](https://substack.com/redirect/77aa2d41-6895-40c1-a771-704b6b5dd611?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[SUPPORT DROP SITE - UPGRADE TODAY!](https://substack.com/redirect/77aa2d41-6895-40c1-a771-704b6b5dd611?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The [20% discount ends Friday](https://substack.com/redirect/77aa2d41-6895-40c1-a771-704b6b5dd611?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). After that, we'll keep pushing to Dec. 11, but this is the fastest way to get us over the line.
See you on the Hill,
Ryan Grim
P.S. If a paid subscription isn't possible right now, that's okay. Keep reading and keep sharing. And if you'd rather not have a recurring payment, [you can make a one-time, tax-deductible donation to help us cross the $100,000 mark instead](https://substack.com/redirect/430f2694-a7a9-4ee5-aafd-857f4a834f85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

memorial’s unfinished list

Hi friends!

🇺🇸 Today, Rocky Mountain Voice says thank you to the men and
women who have served in the United States Armed Forces. Your service
and sacrifice protect the freedoms we enjoy every day, and we are
grateful.

Read Shaina Cole’s piece on Colorado’s veterans, from the 157th
Infantry’s liberation of Dachau to Camp Hale, and on the Colorado
Freedom Memorial, where nearly 3,500 names still lack stories.
Families can share theirs at #TellUsTheirStories. _READ THE FULL
ARTICLE.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

If you see a veteran today, take a moment to say thanks. _HAPPY
VETERANS DAY._

infiltration

through education, media, government and mass illegal immigration; and

Electoral College

TODAY'S TOP STORIES

COLORADO VETERANS: FROM DACHAU TO CAMP HALE, 13 RESOLUTIONS AND A
MEMORIAL’S UNFINISHED LIST
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Colorado voters agreed Tuesday to send $175 million a year to
conservation and

On the morning of April 29, 1945, soldiers of the 157th Infantry
Regiment set foot inside Dachau.

The 157th had Colorado National Guard roots and fought as part of the
U.S. Army’s 45th Infantry Division. House Joint Resolution 26-1011
calls it the Colorado National Guard’s 157th.

The battalion that went in was commanded by Felix Sparks, a
27-year-old lieutenant colonel, who wrote his own accountof the day
decades later. “The initial shock was experienced even before
entering the camp.”

READ MORE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

COLORADO BUILDING PERMITS: SINGLE-FAMILY DOWN NEARLY 43 PERCENT SINCE
2021
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_Colorado’s housing permits are shifting sharply toward large
multi-unit buildings while single-family permits decline, even as
statewide totals rise. Smaller homes also carry substantially higher
costs per bedroom._

*
SINGLE-FAMILY CONSTRUCTION IN STEEP DECLINE: Single-unit permits fell
to 17,406 in 2025 from 20,434 the year before, and are down nearly 43%
since the 2021 peak of 30,246, even as overall permits rose thanks
entirely to buildings with five or more units.

*
SMALLER UNITS COST MORE PER BEDROOM: A Common Sense Institute report
found a one-bedroom home costs about 70% more per bedroom than a
three-bedroom, with studio and one-bedroom rents rising 85% and 73%
respectively since the mid-2010s, far outpacing larger units.

STATE MANDATES FACE LOCAL PUSHBACK: Six Front Range cities sued over
state housing laws establishing a density target of 40 units per acre
in qualifying transit areas and restricting parking mandates, Lakewood
voters repealed their own 2025 zoning ordinances by a 63% margin, and
Littleton voters wrote land-use protections directly into their city
charter.

After losing the 2024 Congressional Election, I initially did not intend to run again. However there were transformational events taking place that changed my mind. I was concerned with the outcome of the Iran War, the continuing rise of antisemitism, the fragmentation of our society, the election of Zohran Mamdani, the policies he instituted and the apparent acceptance of Socialism.
This is in addition to the chronic unsolved problems faced by Connecticut residents:
* congested roads and no plan to fix them
* a stagnant Connecticut economy despite strong growth in other states
* rapidly rising electricity prices
* no plans to meet future demand
* high taxes, poor infrastructure
* wealth and job flight and no evidence that those in power were doing anything significant to make things better.

_**I could not stand by and do nothing. There were no credible candidates seeking the Republican nomination so I decided to step up and run.**_
Republicans winning in Connecticut should have been a no brainer as the facts speak for themselves: _**We have the highest unemployment rate in the country, some of the highest utility rates, some of the highest taxes, some of the highest housing costs and one of the most congested roads I-95**_. Under one party Democrat rule there has been no significant economic growth and our children who want to remain in Connecticut cannot find enough high paying jobs to afford to live here.
Connecticut has passed laws that are jeopardizing the right to own a single family home in a single family neighborhood. The quality of education in Bridgeport and to a lesser extent Norwalk and Stamford is compromised. Charter schools and school vouchers are blocked because of the opposition by the teacher's union. They are powerful supporters of the Democrats and what is good for them takes precedence over what is good for the children.
With all of the problems caused by single party Democrat rule you would think that the voters would be fed up and demand change.
_**I was brought up to believe that if legislators are doing a poor job they should be voted out of office and replaced. To my shock and horror Connecticut voters do not think that way. Instead they choose to re-elect legislators who have failed to solve the problems of Connecticut voters.**_
This outcome is unbelievable. The question is are the voters of Connecticut oblivious to the failure of their elected officials or are they so poisoned by their hatred of Donald Trump that they believe every Republican is a Trump clone who they should hate.
If that is the case, then this is the best con job by a political party in the country. Fail your constituents, shift the blame to Washington, which is not the cause of Connecticut's problems' and not only get re-elected but defeat almost every Republican running for office and create an even larger supermajority
To those who bought this con successfully, I can only say that welcome to two more years of bad laws and bad policies that will only make things worse rather than better in Connecticut.
**As a candidate for the US Congress I saw even more amazing things happen.**
Jim Himes is a great campaigner and he has a great political machine to get out the vote and persuade voters to support him. In our society, voters do not look at the record of who they vote for. Jim votes 95% of the time with the Democrat party. This party is increasingly being dominated by socialists/communists and radical Islamists. Both groups have a different view of America than our founding fathers. Socialism is a failed ideology. There is no socialist country that has a higher standard of living than the US. Almost every American has a cell phone, good internet connection, multiple televisions, and in no urban areas a car. Can you say the same for Communist Cuba, or the once prosperous and now shedding Communism Venezuela, and poverty rates, slave labor and concentration camps are all part of the landscape in China.
At the end of WWII, the Soviet Union controlled Eastern Europe and they were all Communist countries. Once the Soviet Union collapsed these countries shed communism. Israel started out with a significant socialist economy in the form of the kibbutz. It was a third world country. As it converted to a capitalist economy the standard of living rose and it became a first world country.
_**Communists and Socialists work on the theory of division and jealousy. Rich people have more than poor people. They neglect to say that in Communist countries the elite live like kings and everybody else struggles to make a living. However in those societies those that criticize the system are imprisoned or executed. Complainers are silenced.**_
In most countries, you social status is based on your parents. People are born into a certain class and they remain in that class. What is unique to America is that there is an opportunity for those who are born poor to become wealthy. It is an opportunity available to those who have the skills and ambitions to move up. This is unique to American society and it is what has made us the greatest country in the world.
People become wealthy by building businesses or by creating new industries. Their reward is financial success. In the process they create jobs and improve our society and standard of living. The PC, laptop, cell phone, internet, social media, airplanes and cars came into existence because of entrepreneurs who had a dream and made it happen. Success is not guaranteed.
In Socialism there is no reward for innovation or creating new industries so those economies do not grow the same way that ours does. In Socialism bureaucrats not entrepreneurs control industries. They stagnate and are not as efficient. They are less productive and more expensive. People have less and economies stagnate. That is the real truth of socialism.
Socialism appeals to the lazy and the jealous. If that is you, don't be surprised when socialism does not deliver what it promises.
One of the biggest cons concerns college degrees. There is a myth that if you have any college degree you will get a better job than if you don't. Universities have profited on that myth. Students can spend up to $400,000 on an college degree. When you think about it doesn't make sense. In order to get a higher paying job you need a skill that is in demand and requires specialized training to get that skill. For college majors you acquire a specialized skill that will get you a good job. Those skills change as the economy changes. There are other fields that you can major in where there is little demand for your degree.
> One of my campaign issues was "know before you go" which meant that every college and university would have to disclose for every major that they offered a degree, what happened to the students who graduated with that degree. What jobs did they get and what were the starting salaries, what percent even got jobs and what happened to those who were not hired. If you are going to invest four years of your time and up to $400,000 you should know if that investment in time and money made sense. This would also force the universities to gear their curriculum to prepare graduates to meet the needs of employers, not just grant degrees for the sake of granting degrees.
College isn't the only path to a good job. There are tremendous opportunities in the trades that are AI proof. There are shortages of plumbers, electricians, carpenters, HVAC, and other trades that pay comparable if not better salaries than some college degrees. The expenses to get these skills are small. In many trades you start as a paid apprentice and work your way up until you become licensed in that trade.
America is the last superpower that stands between a world dominated by a democracy as opposed to the totalitarian dictatorship of China. When dictatorships dominate the world everyone suffers. When Europe was dominated by the Nazi and Soviet dictatorships during WWII the quality of life for the average person was poor and there were no freedoms. The Japanese dictatorship that dominated Asia during the same period was equally as brutal.
Our quality of life and that of most of the world depends on us remaining the dominant superpower. This happens when we as a country are united, not divided, in the goal of preserving the freedoms granted under our constitution and the preservation of a free enterprise system that is not constrained by government over-regulation or crony capitalism based on a pay to play system.
My run for Congress did not succeed by I will still be there fighting for American democracy and against those who want to destroy it.
Join me in battle. Don't give up. Don't surrender. Spread the world. Together we will win.

clean_body: Some battles are worth fighting--not because victory is certain, but because the issues are too important to ignore. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more The Goldstein Substack - A Father-Son Publication Dr. Goldstein is Running for Congress and his page can be found Some battles are worth fighting--not because victory is certain, but because the issues are too important to ignore. | | | Nov 11 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- After losing the 2024 Congressional Election, I initially did not intend to run again. However there were transformational events taking place that changed my mind. I was concerned with the outcome of the Iran War, the continuing rise of antisemitism, the fragmentation of our society, the election of Zohran Mamdani, the policies he instituted and the apparent acceptance of Socialism. This is in addition to the chronic unsolved problems faced by Connecticut residents: congested roads and no plan to fix them a stagnant Connecticut economy despite strong growth in other states rapidly rising electricity prices no plans to meet future demand high taxes, poor infrastructure wealth and job flight and no evidence that those in power were doing anything significant to make things better. I could not stand by and do nothing. There were no credible candidates seeking the Republican nomination so I decided to step up and run. Republicans winning in Connecticut should have been a no brainer as the facts speak for themselves: We have the highest unemployment rate in the country, some of the highest utility rates, some of the highest taxes, some of the highest housing costs and one of the most congested roads I-95. Under one party Democrat rule there has been no significant economic growth and our children who want to remain in Connecticut cannot find enough high paying jobs to afford to live here. Connecticut has passed laws that are jeopardizing the right to own a single family home in a single family neighborhood. The quality of education in Bridgeport and to a lesser extent Norwalk and Stamford is compromised. Charter schools and school vouchers are blocked because of the opposition by the teacher's union. They are powerful supporters of the Democrats and what is good for them takes precedence over what is good for the children. With all of the problems caused by single party Democrat rule you would think that the voters would be fed up and demand change. I was brought up to believe that if legislators are doing a poor job they should be voted out of office and replaced. To my shock and horror Connecticut voters do not think that way. Instead they choose to re-elect legislators who have failed to solve the problems of Connecticut voters. This outcome is unbelievable. The question is are the voters of Connecticut oblivious to the failure of their elected officials or are they so poisoned by their hatred of Donald Trump that they believe every Republican is a Trump clone who they should hate. If that is the case, then this is the best con job by a political party in the country. Fail your constituents, shift the blame to Washington, which is not the cause of Connecticut's problems' and not only get re-elected but defeat almost every Republican running for office and create an even larger supermajority To those who bought this con successfully, I can only say that welcome to two more years of bad laws and bad policies that will only make things worse rather than better in Connecticut. As a candidate for the US Congress I saw even more amazing things happen. Jim Himes is a great campaigner and he has a great political machine to get out the vote and persuade voters to support him. In our society, voters do not look at the record of who they vote for. Jim votes 95% of the time with the Democrat party. This party is increasingly being dominated by socialists/communists and radical Islamists. Both groups have a different view of America than our founding fathers. Socialism is a failed ideology. There is no socialist country that has a higher standard of living than the US. Almost every American has a cell phone, good internet connection, multiple televisions, and in no urban areas a car. Can you say the same for Communist Cuba, or the once prosperous and now shedding Communism Venezuela, and poverty rates, slave labor and concentration camps are all part of the landscape in China. At the end of WWII, the Soviet Union controlled Eastern Europe and they were all Communist countries. Once the Soviet Union collapsed these countries shed communism. Israel started out with a significant socialist economy in the form of the kibbutz. It was a third world country. As it converted to a capitalist economy the standard of living rose and it became a first world country. Communists and Socialists work on the theory of division and jealousy. Rich people have more than poor people. They neglect to say that in Communist countries the elite live like kings and everybody else struggles to make a living. However in those societies those that criticize the system are imprisoned or executed. Complainers are silenced.** In most countries, you social status is based on your parents. People are born into a certain class and they remain in that class. What is unique to America is that there is an opportunity for those who are born poor to become wealthy. It is an opportunity available to those who have the skills and ambitions to move up. This is unique to American society and it is what has made us the greatest country in the world. People become wealthy by building businesses or by creating new industries. Their reward is financial success. In the process they create jobs and improve our society and standard of living. The PC, laptop, cell phone, internet, social media, airplanes and cars came into existence because of entrepreneurs who had a dream and made it happen. Success is not guaranteed. In Socialism there is no reward for innovation or creating new industries so those economies do not grow the same way that ours does. In Socialism bureaucrats not entrepreneurs control industries. They stagnate and are not as efficient. They are less productive and more expensive. People have less and economies stagnate. That is the real truth of socialism. Socialism appeals to the lazy and the jealous. If that is you, don't be surprised when socialism does not deliver what it promises. One of the biggest cons concerns college degrees. There is a myth that if you have any college degree you will get a better job than if you don't. Universities have profited on that myth. Students can spend up to $400,000 on an college degree. When you think about it doesn't make sense. In order to get a higher paying job you need a skill that is in demand and requires specialized training to get that skill. For college majors you acquire a specialized skill that will get you a good job. Those skills change as the economy changes. There are other fields that you can major in where there is little demand for your degree. One of my campaign issues was "know before you go" which meant that every college and university would have to disclose for every major that they offered a degree, what happened to the students who graduated with that degree. What jobs did they get and what were the starting salaries, what percent even got jobs and what happened to those who were not hired. If you are going to invest four years of your time and up to $400,000 you should know if that investment in time and money made sense. This would also force the universities to gear their curriculum to prepare graduates to meet the needs of employers, not just grant degrees for the sake of granting degrees. College isn't the only path to a good job. There are tremendous opportunities in the trades that are AI proof. There are shortages of plumbers, electricians, carpenters, HVAC, and other trades that pay comparable if not better salaries than some college degrees. The expenses to get these skills are small. In many trades you start as a paid apprentice and work your way up until you become licensed in that trade. America is the last superpower that stands between a world dominated by a democracy as opposed to the totalitarian dictatorship of China. When dictatorships dominate the world everyone suffers. When Europe was dominated by the Nazi and Soviet dictatorships during WWII the quality of life for the average person was poor and there were no freedoms. The Japanese dictatorship that dominated Asia during the same period was equally as brutal. Our quality of life and that of most of the world depends on us remaining the dominant superpower. This happens when we as a country are united, not divided, in the goal of preserving the freedoms granted under our constitution and the preservation of a free enterprise system that is not constrained by government over-regulation or crony capitalism based on a pay to play system. My run for Congress did not succeed by I will still be there fighting for American democracy and against those who want to destroy it. Join me in battle. Don't give up. Don't surrender. Spread the world. Together we will win. The Goldstein Substack is free today. _The midterm election results were nothing short of shocking._

There’s going to be a lot of debate, discussion, and finger-pointing about what happened and why it happened in the coming days and weeks.
---
**But the first step is obvious to everyone: Our Party needs to focus on one thing above all else moving forward...**
---
**We MUST have a better ear for what matters most to _YOU_ – the loyal grassroots patriots who are the backbone of MAGA.**
---

| | Hey Friends!
Democrats have made historic gains, but there is much work to do. Leadership matters and we need bold leadership that will put the people first. I know that many of you understand this and want something new. That is why I am sharing my friend Corbin Trent’s email—it gives you steps to make your voice heard in this upcoming decision. I am just going to post his email below....
In solidarity,Gloria

“Good morning, folks. And a good morning it is. My apologies for any typos. This is a completely dictated, unedited email. I am trying to launch an ad campaign, a massive polling series, and parent 4 kids...But! Pressure is building against leadership. In the United States Senate, we’re seeing more and more senators go on the record saying no to Chuck Schumer. The polling is clear but representatives have a hard time listening once they’re in the swamp. Amazingly, two people: Don Leonard and Angela Gonzalez-Torres have taken the courageous step of saying no to Hakeem. As many of you know, I was the communications director for Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez during her first campaign and then her first term on the Hill. One of the things that made her able to be the independent-minded representative that she was is financial support from a massive number of people. But again, the most important thing we can do is empower the people that stand up and give them a safety net that allows them to take a stand for us the against the powerful people in the party. **A rescue is about to happen.** And somewhere in South America, young women trapped inside a trafficking network may soon have a chance to walk free. They came from several Latin American countries. They were promised **real jobs.** A chance to earn money. **A chance for a better life.** But police say that once these young women were brought under the control of a well-known criminal gang, the promises disappeared. Instead, they were forced into commercial sexual exploitation. **And threatened with violence or death.** Then police went undercover at a brothel tied to the organization. What they found made this even more urgent. Several of the young women they encountered **may be minors**. Now, authorities are preparing to act. **And I am asking you to help us be ready.**

My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I produced the film _Sound of Freedom_ to expose the terrible evil of human trafficking. But making a movie was never enough. That is why we created **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Our mission is simple: **Stop the sale of God 's children.** And right now, we are supporting trusted partners working alongside police and prosecutors as this rescue effort develops. **But there is a serious problem**. Investigators still do not know where the victims are kept when they are not at the brothel.So when police move, the women and girls may be there, or new information may send the team to another location. **Everything can change quickly. **More people may be needed. More time. More transportation. More supplies. And additional help for survivors **after** they are brought to safety. That's why we urgently need to raise **$5,000 to help support this effort with rescue kits for trafficking victims**.

**Peter, rescue is not simply opening a door. ****It is walking with someone through that door.** Our partners stay involved from intelligence and planning through victim recovery, safeguarding, and aftercare. Because leaving the place where you were exploited may only be the first step. A survivor may have nothing. No safe place to sleep. No money. She may fear the traffickers will hurt her family. She may even need help getting safely back to her home country and family. That's why rescue kits can matter so much.

Each kit contains a blanket, hygiene products, snacks, a notebook and pen, and one small item that can become a **lifeline** : **A card with our partner 's contact information.** Not every woman encountered during an operation will leave immediately. Some fear losing belongings hidden elsewhere. Some may have a child being controlled by traffickers. Others fear retaliation against themselves or their families. We never want a woman who is too afraid to leave that day to believe her chance for freedom is gone. **She can hold onto that card. **And when she is ready,**she knows who to call**. That is what your gift builds.
---
* **$25 puts one rescue kit in a survivor's hands.**
* **$50 provides two.**
* **$100 provides four.**
* **$250 provides ten** **-- enough for an entire operation**.

---

name: Wally King, American Veterans Center
subject: I was a POW for two weeks
body:
My commander was right. Just not the way either of us meant.

My commander was right. Just not the way either of us meant.
| | | |
---
Friend,
---
On April 18, 1945, I walked up to my squadron commander and said, "This is my 75th mission. Don't you think it's time to quit?"He said, "Yeah. This is going to be your last mission."He was right. _Just not the way either of us meant._ My name is Wally King. I just turned 103. During World War II, I flew P-47 Thunderbolts over France and Germany with the 513th Fighter Squadron.
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkbGO2zAMhp9G3s4QJZ-dGzQUCLxdh6JAR4GhGEeIZbmUHL9-4Uu2TreSP78fH_jn039inOMy_cTETurVS_Fxx4Jr3q9Z6p535nvxRpv-DeANwCPV-GDfYRNcoIBADTsYPrrO6hP0zc0Fq3saUAfCywksBNufBkt0GQzTOw9NdAcPAMCA1vDefnR24JPW14vV1hhSncaZpbbC63aZI-FSsdyvWYhbyqmZ3a3WtSj7Q5lRmbEwbcItJpYj_ODKgkshXipLm2VSZpw2LtWXOC0sTyOP9FfZseRNiD3lwMqef_0eoTedMcr0W00-cYhbUvbMCeP8Gj5PlD3fUAKW-xfpuSJMK8ZpUfaMD_L_t75yleWgNuLCusd5jqUfVKeno-XLsX77IQ9n_gUAAP__la-dAA)
---
I grew up in rural Ohio. I went to all 12 grades in the same school building, and my graduating class had 32 students. All 16 of the boys served in the war.I'd wanted to fly since I was a kid building model airplanes. The P-47 was a tough, honest airplane. It could take a beating and bring you home.The mission I remember most came just before Christmas 1944, during the Battle of the Bulge.Our job was to knock out the German guns around Bastogne before the supply planes came in. Everything was buried in snow.When the parachutes dropped, men who had been dug in under all that white came up out of the ground and started dragging those supplies into town.**Friend, I'll never forget that sight.** _Then came April 18._ On the way home, my wingman spotted a gun on a railroad car, and we went down for a look. Flak hit my engine. Fire came over the windshield.I bailed out over German territory with civilians shooting at me on the way down.Friend, I was beaten, burned and terrified. I'd never given God much thought before that day, but right then, a peace came over me like nothing I'd ever felt. It stayed with me the whole two weeks I was a prisoner.**And it was a German doctor who got me home.** He was caring for badly wounded Americans in a house near the Russian front. When the war was all but over, he rode with us in two ambulances to the American lines, driving after midnight with no lights.I've often wondered how many of those boys would have lived without him.
