For years now, I've talked to students about the war.**What troubles me, Friend, is how little young Americans know about World War II.** When students ask me for advice, I tell them: _put down your cell phones and love one another._ But I can't get to every classroom, Friend.**That's why I'm writing to you on behalf of the American Veterans Center. They make sure the next generation hears the truth from the people who lived it.** AVC is a nonprofit educational organization dedicated to preserving and promoting the legacy of America's veterans and active-duty service members, from World War II through today. Its work includes:
---
* **The National Memorial Day Parade** in Washington, D.C., the nation's largest Memorial Day event
* **The Annual Veterans Conference** every Veterans Day weekend, where veterans of every generation share their stories with hundreds of cadets and midshipmen
* **AMERICAN VALOR: A Salute to Our Heroes,** a two-time Emmy-winning special broadcast nationwide
* **Oral histories and documentaries** that record veterans' stories in their own words, so they're never lost

---

clean_body: My commander was right. Just not the way either of us meant. My commander was right. Just not the way either of us meant. | | | | Friend, On April 18, 1945, I walked up to my squadron commander and said, "This is my 75th mission. Don't you think it's time to quit?"He said, "Yeah. This is going to be your last mission."He was right. Just not the way either of us meant. My name is Wally King. I just turned 103. During World War II, I flew P-47 Thunderbolts over France and Germany with the 513th Fighter Squadron. I grew up in rural Ohio. I went to all 12 grades in the same school building, and my graduating class had 32 students. All 16 of the boys served in the war.I'd wanted to fly since I was a kid building model airplanes. The P-47 was a tough, honest airplane. It could take a beating and bring you home.The mission I remember most came just before Christmas 1944, during the Battle of the Bulge.Our job was to knock out the German guns around Bastogne before the supply planes came in. Everything was buried in snow.When the parachutes dropped, men who had been dug in under all that white came up out of the ground and started dragging those supplies into town.Friend, I'll never forget that sight. Then came April 18. On the way home, my wingman spotted a gun on a railroad car, and we went down for a look. Flak hit my engine. Fire came over the windshield.I bailed out over German territory with civilians shooting at me on the way down.Friend, I was beaten, burned and terrified. I'd never given God much thought before that day, but right then, a peace came over me like nothing I'd ever felt. It stayed with me the whole two weeks I was a prisoner.And it was a German doctor who got me home. He was caring for badly wounded Americans in a house near the Russian front. When the war was all but over, he rode with us in two ambulances to the American lines, driving after midnight with no lights.I've often wondered how many of those boys would have lived without him. Above: I met with the boys of the 117 th Air Refueling Wing of the Alabama National Guard before flying to Normandy, France in June 2025 for the 81 st anniversary of D-Day. For years now, I've talked to students about the war.What troubles me, Friend, is how little young Americans know about World War II. When students ask me for advice, I tell them: put down your cell phones and love one another. But I can't get to every classroom, Friend.That's why I'm writing to you on behalf of the American Veterans Center. They make sure the next generation hears the truth from the people who lived it. AVC is a nonprofit educational organization dedicated to preserving and promoting the legacy of America's veterans and active-duty service members, from World War II through today. Its work includes: The National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C., the nation's largest Memorial Day event The Annual Veterans Conference every Veterans Day weekend, where veterans of every generation share their stories with hundreds of cadets and midshipmen AMERICAN VALOR: A Salute to Our Heroes, a two-time Emmy-winning special broadcast nationwide Oral histories and documentaries that record veterans' stories in their own words, so they're never lost AVC is funded entirely by people like you, and every gift is tax-deductible. Thank you for listening to an old pilot - and for taking the time to consider supporting the American Veterans Center. I hope you'll join them on this mission to honor our veterans by preserving and promoting their legacies of service and sacrifice. Wally King First Lieutenant, U.S. Army Air Forces 513th Fighter Squadron, 406th Fighter Group, Ninth Air ForceOn behalf of American Veterans Center, P.S. Friend, my commander promised me one last mission back in 1945. Peter, In the 2026 midterms, the National Democratic Redistricting Committee ran one of our most ambitious electoral programs ever — because our democracy was up against some of its greatest threats ever. We had a massive job ahead of us. We needed to elect Democracy Defenders — to key state-level offices with power over redistricting and voting rights — so we can deliver fair maps and fair access to the ballot across the country. We endorsed a slew of strong, pro-democracy candidates. Supporters like you stepped up to support their campaigns. And — while votes are still being counted in many states — we know so far you helped deliver over 200 victories, including: Electing seven governors. Electing 197 state legislators, which fundamentally shifted power in several states across the country. Sweeping all four targeted state supreme court races. Winning two critical ballot measures — one in Missouri, where voters rejected a new GOP gerrymander, and one in Maryland, where voters have now let state officials respond to the Republican redistricting crisis. Those numbers won’t go anywhere but up as more ballots get counted and more races get called. And that’s all on top of the political earthquake across the country. Republicans had launched a redistricting crisis to try to hold onto the House — no matter what the American people had to say about it. But the fair maps movement fought back ferociously and strategically. And the American people were able to make their voices heard. They were able to elect a Democratic House. And Americans were so outraged by the Trump GOP’s chaos, corruption, and destruction that they flipped the Senate from red to blue, too. Thank you for powering victories for our democracy across the country, up and down the ballot. We’re grateful that you’re part of the fair maps movement as we face down new gerrymandering attempts — which could be imminent in places like Mississippi before January — and new attacks on our democracy. Stephen Miller just got one of the most powerful jobs in the White House, and Republicans are already turning on him. Trump thinks doubling down on his most extreme policies is the answer to a devastating election. But behind closed doors, even his own people are sounding the alarm.
And it gets worse. We have Republican lawmakers openly calling for Miller's firing, former classmates dragging him publicly, and new polling showing just how unpopular this decision really is. This one is a mess, folks.

name: Wally King, American Veterans Center
subject: 75 missions
body:
From rural Ohio to Normandy, France
My commander was right. Just not the way either of us meant.

| | | | [](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=bfd1236259d84f9ead4fe25b7639e27d&_e=2T6bxhw7QE1GSz4eICsrk-gWGalL9V2sqRBuKGnYXluD_T3TtaCVQ8IQFayuUnS50J2dM2D647ZvrjpTXCjNtlvJDWsuxwUPbTSd2doqzJAcz9S9PeNOx3vjzJf4kbwTaqkY5NyC3_fGdHVXaJH08Z396l_VaL1sozHI07cImy7Seer8hEKLtKEZhVuyivz-QSQD2NNjaPUgApryX3qM9m_bgYfuFhLo_XdAvBDM38o7mTI3UynUBIp5ZWWVOjvM_1wIAyQ7RPurVWi97-KTE87xGdradWu6ZMJAjViuisDcIGpd4X1aUNlFukrmNEaWjdJUs809D1BwFSuBUTdW17II51Aqv116dWG6VQBVI0tUAjor4J2Pzx5wp_zzMrI5vxPwyZwACuTqI-po14mwS0w8fwHV76_KLwRVl9QHHyu5oJWXuRjqiwPnymg9CAJQyJzDwLHLLPhT7x2oY0du4rUlhnjpCDJET80AyrdCOzFsASZS1DErUKuCL7Jw36iKitBuZI2BojG5MHdsohTCKSz5Zanldw0esfmK6I1PxziBtGp7JJHNR7ufWxia__duCRdu1KBkjDGnqLzVvQ3S0yYXX9z96Xcu2OYBsvlr4MZLWLmKKN4gS07DKU7q7Sa2MjsR3qiLc1HxSB9GqBKorQ5qTkhitnVKumgWPAXOAB6maJtiQjR1Kujwqzxesqb6k2Z28L2uZyN5wBsH47qSEQ%3D%3D)
---
Peter,
---
On April 18, 1945, I walked up to my squadron commander and said, "This is my 75th mission. Don't you think it's time to quit?"He said, "Yeah. This is going to be your last mission."He was right. _Just not the way either of us meant._ My name is Wally King. I just turned 103. During World War II, I flew P-47 Thunderbolts over France and Germany with the 513th Fighter Squadron.
---
[](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=bfd1236259d84f9ead4fe25b7639e27d&_e=2T6bxhw7QE1GSz4eICsrk-gWGalL9V2sqRBuKGnYXluD_T3TtaCVQ8IQFayuUnS50J2dM2D647ZvrjpTXCjNtlvJDWsuxwUPbTSd2doqzJAcz9S9PeNOx3vjzJf4kbwTaqkY5NyC3_fGdHVXaJH08Z396l_VaL1sozHI07cImy7Seer8hEKLtKEZhVuyivz-QSQD2NNjaPUgApryX3qM9m_bgYfuFhLo_XdAvBDM38o7mTI3UynUBIp5ZWWVOjvM-1uYshZ3LYiHM8I1XmKzZjd9ie9nAEkU0Gje1q1IRv-qkDh4k-x8Ph3k0zbL9DD0TNIqYJ1RX03gqpDPo7hSbzvpN6O6qKlPtE8t-6cQgOCxRIEc768HQ4A_bHgjGeSBvXqMPpOcrKsJ5dqWjbNSCxmDpbjR6CEZq1D9p_AHZCfF50beTar9M2wSUkBuwqF4JCyXz0KKM-saAzFQtcazz1vQK6ZxbVKcEFE-rPEAfwxXtTcR508NK-OJ0-SAJy4AcHoLe5FjkXkXYKvfeThaDarSaqJ-POIpfjJlnlwcwkylbvGXh9MWiylSOy1OyAyGUXmW12cST7nIepwQMrfi2P1fuxRe4ALvBeuZd57lhEld0E2CEUw5nesi6QzQZP4jFXsoRF7sJ5oSE8paM-GWI9s1S0vgiQ8I88o9GUYa4tss6yeDfSy85VOty9TE20zDKrzj-9wAg7CnVxSmdbGDlQ%3D%3D)
---
I grew up in rural Ohio. I went to all 12 grades in the same school building, and my graduating class had 32 students. All 16 of the boys served in the war.I'd wanted to fly since I was a kid building model airplanes. The P-47 was a tough, honest airplane. It could take a beating and bring you home.The mission I remember most came just before Christmas 1944, during the Battle of the Bulge.Our job was to knock out the German guns around Bastogne before the supply planes came in. Everything was buried in snow.When the parachutes dropped, men who had been dug in under all that white came up out of the ground and started dragging those supplies into town.**Peter, I'll never forget that sight.** _Then came April 18._ On the way home, my wingman spotted a gun on a railroad car, and we went down for a look. Flak hit my engine. Fire came over the windshield.I bailed out over German territory with civilians shooting at me on the way down.Peter, I was beaten, burned and terrified. I'd never given God much thought before that day, but right then, a peace came over me like nothing I'd ever felt. It stayed with me the whole two weeks I was a prisoner.**And it was a German doctor who got me home.** He was caring for badly wounded Americans in a house near the Russian front. When the war was all but over, he rode with us in two ambulances to the American lines, driving after midnight with no lights.I've often wondered how many of those boys would have lived without him.

Everyone is still reeling from the horrifying outcome of the midterms, with the ship of state feeling like it hit the _Titanic_ of electoral outcomes. Every bad policy that has run aground in blue states now threatens to sink the whole country.
A potential permanent impact of Tuesday's election results is that Democrats now control enough state legislatures to reach more than 270 electoral votes. This could allow them to enact the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact. If the Compact is ruled constitutional, it would effectively nullify the Electoral College by awarding participating states' electoral votes to the national popular vote winner.
In layman's terms, the Compact is legislation that directs a state's electors to award their Electoral College votes to the winner of the national popular vote, regardless of how their own state voted.
Before Tuesday's election, Democrats held 222 electoral votes at the state level through jurisdictions that had already joined the Compact. After Democrats won control of Pennsylvania (19 electoral votes), Michigan (15), Arizona (11), Wisconsin (10), and Nevada (6), they now control a total of 283 electoral votes--well above the 270 threshold needed to activate the Compact.
Now two major questions remain: Will Democrats attempt to pass the Compact in these newly controlled state legislatures, and if passed, will the Supreme Court rule the Compact constitutional?
First, let's break down the new state legislatures that Democrats control:
## **Michigan**
Senate Majority Leader Darrin Camilleri and House Speaker-elect Ranjeev Puri were selected by their caucuses to[ lead](https://substack.com/redirect/93d26a62-f28f-4661-9974-4f3d388601fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the new Democratic majorities in Lansing. Rep. Ranjeev Puri cosponsored House Bill 6213, the National Popular Vote bill introduced in the Michigan House on July 3, 2026, and has been associated with earlier NPV efforts during the prior Democrat trifecta.
Keep in mind, Michigan voters just decided it is better to send to the US Senate a man with known ties to terrorism rather than a war hero.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/aacb8953-1a7e-4293-ae25-ead306673768?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/54d710e0-16f5-4eb8-9d59-88d87ab7de1b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## **Arizona**
Senate Democratic Leader Priya Sundareshan and House Democratic Leader Oscar De Los Santos, two fine American names there, are the expected [leaders ](https://substack.com/redirect/c0bc8e87-baf9-4ad5-8c09-e46ae936d8b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)of the new Democratic majorities. Sundareshan cosponsored the National Popular Vote bill (SB 1300) introduced in the Arizona Senate in 2026 by Sen. Rosanna Gabaldon, and has been listed as a sponsor or cosponsor on earlier NPV legislation (including 2023 bills).

---|---|---
## **Wisconsin**
Senate Minority Leader (expected Majority Leader) Dianne Hesselbein and Assembly Minority Leader (expected Speaker) Greta Neubauer are the projected[ leaders](https://substack.com/redirect/c0bc8e87-baf9-4ad5-8c09-e46ae936d8b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Rep. Greta Neubauer cosponsored Assembly Bill 1152 (introduced March 13, 2026), the National Popular Vote bill in the Wisconsin Assembly, as well as earlier versions including AB 246 in 2021 and AB 185 in 2019. Hesselbein cosponsored the companion Senate measure.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bc87864f-1013-498d-9e7d-32c72cc3e31d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## **Nevada**
Senate Majority Leader Edgar Flores was selected to lead the Democratic Senate majority. Assembly Speaker Steve Yeager is expected to continue in a [leadership](https://substack.com/redirect/5cf06752-daba-4c43-8226-0fce11615fdb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) role. Flores was listed as a joint sponsor of Assembly Joint Resolution 6 (AJR 6) in 2023, which sought to place the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact into the Nevada Constitution.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a89aad26-7690-4ea9-9549-6591070147f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## **Pennsylvania**
House Speaker Joanna McClinton, Senate Democratic Leader Jay Costa (in line for president pro tempore), and House Majority Leader Matt Bradford lead the new Democratic trifecta in Harrisburg. None of the current [leadership](https://substack.com/redirect/0fa8b027-451e-422a-b7b2-860c71b9a76a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has cosponsored National Popular Vote legislation. However, the prospects of the Compact have been mentioned before, including a 2025 co-sponsorship memo for NPV legislation (HB 270) circulated by other Democrats such as Rep. Christopher Rabb.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d094ad65-3b74-4abe-9cde-2f9f3437c98d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now, let's say for the sake of argument that the states above all pass the Compact. What happens next? It is likely that the next step would be an emergency hearing and ruling by the United States Supreme Court. Given that states would be fighting each other over elections, the Court would likely use this factor as justification to take up the case.
Given the Court's 6-3 conservative majority, it is likely the Court will rule the Democrats' efforts unconstitutional under the Interstate Compact Clause of the Constitution, which requires congressional consent for certain interstate agreements. However, this outcome is far from certain, and the fact that this is even up for debate means it could simply be a question of when, not if, Democrats start rewriting the Constitution like this.
Democrats have long had the goal of sabotaging the Electoral College, even though President Trump won both the popular and electoral vote in 2024.
So, to answer the question about the Electoral College being effectively canceled before 2028, the answer is: buckle up. Things are about to get very bumpy.

Peter,

On April 18, 1945, I walked up to my squadron commander and said, "This is my 75th mission. Don't you think it's time to quit?"He said, "Yeah. This is going to be your last mission."He was right. _Just not the way either of us meant._ My name is Wally King. I just turned 103. During World War II, I flew P-47 Thunderbolts over France and Germany with the 513th Fighter Squadron.

I grew up in rural Ohio. I went to all 12 grades in the same school building, and my graduating class had 32 students. All 16 of the boys served in the war.I'd wanted to fly since I was a kid building model airplanes. The P-47 was a tough, honest airplane. It could take a beating and bring you home.The mission I remember most came just before Christmas 1944, during the Battle of the Bulge.Our job was to knock out the German guns around Bastogne before the supply planes came in. Everything was buried in snow.When the parachutes dropped, men who had been dug in under all that white came up out of the ground and started dragging those supplies into town.**Peter, I'll never forget that sight.** _Then came April 18._ On the way home, my wingman spotted a gun on a railroad car, and we went down for a look. Flak hit my engine. Fire came over the windshield.I bailed out over German territory with civilians shooting at me on the way down.Peter, I was beaten, burned and terrified. I'd never given God much thought before that day, but right then, a peace came over me like nothing I'd ever felt. It stayed with me the whole two weeks I was a prisoner.**And it was a German doctor who got me home.** He was caring for badly wounded Americans in a house near the Russian front. When the war was all but over, he rode with us in two ambulances to the American lines, driving after midnight with no lights.I've often wondered how many of those boys would have lived without him.

For years now, I've talked to students about the war.**What troubles me, Peter, is how little young Americans know about World War II.** When students ask me for advice, I tell them: _put down your cell phones and love one another._ But I can't get to every classroom, Peter.**That's why I'm writing to you on behalf of the American Veterans Center. They make sure the next generation hears the truth from the people who lived it.** AVC is a nonprofit educational organization dedicated to preserving and promoting the legacy of America's veterans and active-duty service members, from World War II through today. Its work includes:
---
* **The National Memorial Day Parade** in Washington, D.C., the nation's largest Memorial Day event
* **The Annual Veterans Conference** every Veterans Day weekend, where veterans of every generation share their stories with hundreds of cadets and midshipmen
* **AMERICAN VALOR: A Salute to Our Heroes,** a two-time Emmy-winning special broadcast nationwide

clean_body: My commander was right. Just not the way either of us meant. | | | | Peter, On April 18, 1945, I walked up to my squadron commander and said, "This is my 75th mission. Don't you think it's time to quit?"He said, "Yeah. This is going to be your last mission."He was right. Just not the way either of us meant. My name is Wally King. I just turned 103. During World War II, I flew P-47 Thunderbolts over France and Germany with the 513th Fighter Squadron. I grew up in rural Ohio. I went to all 12 grades in the same school building, and my graduating class had 32 students. All 16 of the boys served in the war.I'd wanted to fly since I was a kid building model airplanes. The P-47 was a tough, honest airplane. It could take a beating and bring you home.The mission I remember most came just before Christmas 1944, during the Battle of the Bulge.Our job was to knock out the German guns around Bastogne before the supply planes came in. Everything was buried in snow.When the parachutes dropped, men who had been dug in under all that white came up out of the ground and started dragging those supplies into town.Peter, I'll never forget that sight. Then came April 18. On the way home, my wingman spotted a gun on a railroad car, and we went down for a look. Flak hit my engine. Fire came over the windshield.I bailed out over German territory with civilians shooting at me on the way down.Peter, I was beaten, burned and terrified. I'd never given God much thought before that day, but right then, a peace came over me like nothing I'd ever felt. It stayed with me the whole two weeks I was a prisoner.And it was a German doctor who got me home. He was caring for badly wounded Americans in a house near the Russian front. When the war was all but over, he rode with us in two ambulances to the American lines, driving after midnight with no lights.I've often wondered how many of those boys would have lived without him. Above: I met with the boys of the 117 th Air Refueling Wing of the Alabama National Guard before flying to Normandy, France in June 2025 for the 81 st anniversary of D-Day. For years now, I've talked to students about the war.What troubles me, Peter, is how little young Americans know about World War II. When students ask me for advice, I tell them: put down your cell phones and love one another. But I can't get to every classroom, Peter.That's why I'm writing to you on behalf of the American Veterans Center. They make sure the next generation hears the truth from the people who lived it. AVC is a nonprofit educational organization dedicated to preserving and promoting the legacy of America's veterans and active-duty service members, from World War II through today. Its work includes: The National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C., the nation's largest Memorial Day event The Annual Veterans Conference every Veterans Day weekend, where veterans of every generation share their stories with hundreds of cadets and midshipmen AMERICAN VALOR: A Salute to Our Heroes, a two-time Emmy-winning special broadcast nationwide Oral histories and documentaries that record veterans' stories in their own words, so they're never lost AVC is funded entirely by people like you, and every gift is tax-deductible. Thank you for listening to an old pilot - and for taking the time to consider supporting the American Veterans Center. I hope you'll join them on this mission to honor our veterans by preserving and promoting their legacies of service and sacrifice. I am forever grateful for the people in our family who have served, especially my dad, who was an Army Captain stationed in Germany and New Orleans during the Vietnam War. He still shares experiences from the immense responsibility he had to notify next of kin and how that shaped the rest of his life.

Stefany

| | | Dear Friends, From the bottom of my heart, thank you. While Tuesday's election did not bring the outcome we had hoped for, I am incredibly proud of the campaign we ran and deeply grateful to everyone who made it possible. Over the past several months, I traveled across all 62 counties, meeting New Yorkers who shared their concerns, hopes, and ideas for the future of our state. Those conversations will stay with me long after this election. To our donors, volunteers, supporters, and everyone who believed in our campaign, your generosity, hard work, and encouragement meant more than words can express. Although we came up short, the issues we raised remain important. My commitment to public safety, accountability, and a better future for New York's children has not changed. Serving as your candidate for Attorney General has been an extraordinary privilege, and I will carry the lessons of this experience with me for years to come. With heartfelt gratitude, Saritha Komatireddy

| | | Her name is Luka Hein. She was **16 years old** when doctors removed her breasts. **Now she wants a jury to hear what happened to her. **But getting Luka into that courtroom has become a battle of its own. I'm Mark Trammell, CEO of the**Center for American Liberty** , a nonprofit public interest law firm that takes on cases many organizations won't touch. And I'm asking you to help us fight for Luka.

As we described in her lawsuit, Luka was a deeply troubled teenager. Her parents had divorced. She struggled with anxiety, isolation, school, panic attacks, self-harm, and thoughts of suicide. Then she encountered transgender influencers online. At 15, Luka began receiving gender-related care. At 16, doctors removed her breasts. Testosterone came months later. Luka now alleges that the medical professionals who treated her failed to provide the proper standard of care and failed to obtain informed consent. **Her case is headed toward a jury trial currently scheduled for June, 2027.** **But the legal battle is already raging. **Right now, the defendants are challenging expert testimony Luka intends to present regarding the standard of care. **These kinds of fights mean more motions, more legal work, more time, and more expense. **

And that can become a strategy all its own -- **make litigation so long and expensive that the other side runs out of resources. ****We refuse to let that happen. **We've been here before. The **Center for American Liberty** represents detransitioner **Chloe Cole** in her lawsuit against the medical providers she alleged harmed her. The hospital defendants aggressively filed motions delaying Chloe's trial by years. ## That didn't take long...
Barely a week after the Democrats' victory at the federal and state level in Texas, the mayor of Houston announced on Friday he is issuing an executive order to limit the Houston Police Department's cooperation with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
The executive order bans HPD officers from contacting ICE "for nonviolent offenses, helping reduce fear in our communities. Thank you to Chief Diaz, our state and local leaders for their collaboration. A step toward building a stronger Houston."
[| | | | | Houston Mayor's Office
---
@houmayor
I have signed an executive order directing HPD to no longer contact ICE for nonviolent offences, helping reduce fear in our communities. Thank you to Chief Diaz, our state and local leaders for their collaboration. A step toward building a stronger Houston. Let's Go to Work.
| 5:53 PM * Nov 6, 2026 * 2M Views8.36K Replies * 1.35K Reposts * 6.11K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/dbff3490-eb3d-4f41-ab43-8051f0f1d44a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Houston had to be reminded of the necessity of working with ICE by Governor Greg Abbott as Houston's residents increasingly demanded for the city to stop its partnership. But now that the new incoming Democrat governor, Gina Hinojosa, has voiced opposition for such a partnership, it is safe to say this new executive order will stay in place.
Responding to Mayor John Whitmire's announcement, ICE explained some of the horrific crimes that are considered "nonviolent."
[| | | | | U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement
---
@ICEgov
Watching child porn and selling heroin are classified as "nonviolent offenses" by the way. This is the Mayor of Houston directly advocating for policies that protect some of the worst criminals in America.
| | | | | Houston Mayor's Office @houmayor
---|---|---

It can be sure that Whitmire's new policy for working with ICE is the start of other Texas localities following suit. The Lone Star State will start becoming the Lone Star Sanctuary State and will require the Department of Homeland Security to allocate more resources and manpower to the region.
To say this will be a big blow to Trump's immigration policy is an understatement. Texas has been helping with immigration enforcement since Operation Lone Star during the Biden-Harris border crisis. This massive operation has continued under the second Trump administration, although in a different fashion since tens of thousands of illegal immigrants are no longer crossing on a daily basis.
It should therefore not be surprising that Hinojosa is against it. She has not addressed the state's operation since winning on Tuesday, but it would not be shocking if she starts the process to end it once she enters office.
_**(Piece continues below)**_
* * *
# **We will not give up hope, and neither should you**
Tuesday was a wake up call to all American patriots...
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f33d92fb-159c-461e-ace9-082104d1f035?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

The battle ahead will surely be hard and up-hill. But think of the brave Americans who stormed the beaches of Normandy, or the men who fought and bled at Shiloh and Lexington.
They had a dream for America they were willing to die for. We cannot let their sacrifice be in vain.
We must fight for our nation with every thing we have within us, even on the darkest days, as our ancestors did.
**PolitiBrawl will hold our place in line on the battleground for information and news.**
We appreciate your readership and support.
Do not give up hope. Tomorrow is a brighter day.
* * *
_**(Piece continues):**_
Operation Lone Star is currently budgeted until next summer.
This is why for the swing voters or Republicans who either did not vote or voted for Democrats because they believed Trump was not keeping his deportation promise makes no sense. Also, this path will do nothing to address the high cost of living.
Not only will it be harder to fund DHS once the current budget runs out at the end of Trump's turn, but Democrats being in charge of the biggest border state will only guarantee that the illegal immigrant population will feel more secure.
The worst case scenario is a Democrat winning the White House in 2028, undoing Trump's immigration policies again, and the southern border experiencing another crisis, but this time without Texas filling in the gaps. I did many ride-alongs with Texas state troopers during the Biden administration and they were critical in doing what they can to confront the massive problem.
It is not a foregone conclusion, but the U.S. is certainly closer to having a repeat of Biden Border Crisis 2.0 than it was before the midterms.
